capabilities_declared.description: The capabilities a remedy declares for its need (Workflow #411 B15).

remedy_source.description: The source that decided a remedy's allowed capabilities or a parameter's value: the target record, the configuration or the package default (Workflow #411 B15).

remedy_problem.description: Why a remedy cannot be used, or why a blocked task stopped for a person (Workflow #411 B15).

remedy_depth.description: The layer of a remedy chain, 1 to 3; layer 1 is the remedy of the round's root blocked task (Workflow #411 B15).

decision_id.description: A policy dispatch decision's identifier; for a remedy, the decision of the blocked run that opened the round (Workflow #411 B15).

irreversible.description: True when a provider of the capability on the instance declares it irreversible (Workflow #411 B15).

remedy_inputs_digest.description: The SHA-256 over the inputs of a remedy decision on one instance: the versions of the target records that apply, the configuration rows in effect, the remedy table entries of the blocked mapping and of every provider of its capabilities, and the active catalog hash; a different value lifts a stop. It hashes declarations and versions, never a package's content (Workflow #411 B15).

parameter_name.description: A parameter a provider package declares for a capability (Workflow #411 B15).

parameter_value.description: A parameter's value: one of the options its provider package declares (Workflow #411 B15).

run_parameters.description: The read-only parameters a dispatch hands to its run, one record each: the name, the resolved value and the source that gave it (Workflow #411 B15).

step.description: The step of actinglab resource verify a result belongs to (Workflow #411 RV-1).

step_count.description: How many steps a run of actinglab resource verify ran (Workflow #411 RV-1).

failed_step_count.description: How many steps of a run of actinglab resource verify failed (Workflow #411 RV-1).

git_command.description: The read-only git command that failed (Workflow #411 RV-1).

repo.description: The repository checkout a command was given (Workflow #411 RV-1).

checkout_problem.description: Why a checkout is not the commit to verify (Workflow #411 RV-1).

path_count.description: How many paths share the problem (Workflow #411 RV-1).

first_path.description: The first of those paths, relative to the repository root (Workflow #411 RV-1).

dirty_problem.description: How a checkout differs from its commit's tree (Workflow #411 RV-1).

base.description: A base revision as it was given (Workflow #411 RV-1).

base_problem.description: Why a base revision is refused (Workflow #411 RV-1).

tools_problem.description: What the build manifest beside the executable does not confirm (Workflow #411 RV-1).

layout_problem.description: Which rule of a bundle source a repository breaks (Workflow #411 RV-1).

bundle_problem.description: How a written bundle differs from its source (Workflow #411 RV-1).

readback_problem.description: How a written zip reads back (Workflow #411 RV-1).

found_after_first.description: The failure was found after its step's first failure, by validating each remaining path on its own (Workflow #411 RV-1).

unformatted.description: The files of a content directory that are not in the canonical serialization, each a /-separated path relative to that directory, not an absolute path (Workflow #411 RV-1).

fact_time_problem.description: Why a fact_time_reached predicate's fact gives no time (Workflow #405).

due_at_unix_ms.description: When a task first became due for dispatch, in Unix milliseconds (Workflow #405).

random_delay_ms.description: The random delay drawn for a dispatch, in milliseconds (Workflow #405).

why.description: Why a candidate that a dispatch decision record names did not run: the last reason of its scheduling decision, the one that settled it, never none (Workflow #411 A26; contracts/scheduling/README.md, "Why A Candidate Does Not Run").

decision_state.description: The state of the scheduling decision of a candidate that a dispatch decision record lists (Workflow #411 A26).

eligibility.description: The eligibility of the scheduling decision of a candidate that a dispatch decision record lists: what its trigger and feedback stop decided (Workflow #411 A26).

omitted_why.description: The candidates of the same instance that a dispatch decision record does not list, counted by why: one record per code, in ascending code order (Workflow #411 A26).

program_problem.description: Which rule of a contained task's program refused it at admission (Workflow #411 A39).

expected_target_type.description: The kind of id a Lab operation's target must be (#411 A37).

received_target_type.description: The kind of id a Lab operation's target was (#411 A37).

lab_operation_problem.description: Why the Lab cannot run the operation a package declares, as the kernel runs it (Workflow #412 B-3).

last_in_window.description: The dispatch is the last round of its activity window: no clock of its task's trigger occurs again before the window ends (Workflow #411 B8).

last_daily_slot.description: The dispatch is the last of today's budget: the daily budgets of its task and activity profile allow no further run in the activity day (Workflow #411 B8).

daily_remaining.description: The runs the daily budgets of a task and its activity profile still allow in the activity day after this dispatch (Workflow #411 B8).

run_cap.description: The runs a dispatch's spend allowances pay for: the least, over the consumed pools its task reserves, of the allowance divided by the task's declared consumption of the pool per run, rounded down; when no produced pool of the task carries a base weight, at most the runs its largest open goal gap still needs; and at most 1000, the ceiling of a max_repeats fact cap (SS-6).

effect_index.description: The position, from 0, of an entry in a task's own consumes or produces list of the scheduling catalog (SS-6).

spend_allowance.description: How much of a pool a dispatch may spend, in the pool's real units: the reserve gate's available amount at the evaluation (the pool's projected amount less the other tasks' consumption its latest reading does not show yet) less the task's reserve on it, at least 0 (SS-6).

gap_remaining.description: The gap of the active resource goal on a pool a task produces, in the pool's real units, at the evaluation; 0 when the goal is met (SS-6).

spend_allowances.description: The spend allowances a dispatch hands its run, one record per entry of its task's consumes whose pool the task also reserves, in list order: the entry's position and the allowance (SS-6).

gaps_remaining.description: The remaining goal gaps a dispatch hands its run, one record per entry of its task's produces whose pool an active goal covering the task holds with a known gap, in list order: the entry's position and the gap (SS-6).

argument_value.description: The value an MCP tool argument was given, verbatim, where the argument's refusal names it: for a list argument, the one element refused (Workflow #411 B27).

expected_shape.description: The shape a declaration member must have, where the declaration check refused the member, or an element of it, for its type and the grammar names the shape (Workflow #411 B28).

box_x.description: The left edge of a click box, in the coordinate space of its task, pixels (Workflow #411 B34).

box_y.description: The top edge of a click box, in the coordinate space of its task, pixels (Workflow #411 B34).

box_width.description: The width of a click box, pixels; a point click's box is 1 wide (Workflow #411 B34).

box_height.description: The height of a click box, pixels; a point click's box is 1 high (Workflow #411 B34).

layer_outcome_key.description: The outcome key of the scheduling outcome mapping a prerequisite layer's run ended on, as the layer's package declares it (Workflow #411 B39).

pool_id.description: The id of a resource pool of the scheduling catalog (Workflow #411 B16).

reserve_at_least.description: The least amount, in the pool's real units, that a task's catalog reserve says the pool must still hold after a run of the task (Workflow #411 B16).

amount_after.description: The amount, in the pool's real units, that the pool would hold after a run of the task: its projected amount less the task's declared consumption and less any consumption that goes first; negative when the consumption exceeds the amount (Workflow #411 B16).

predecessor_task_id.description: The task a dependency_completed predicate names: the predecessor whose terminal state it reads (SCH-M CF-1).

served_by_dispatch_unix_ms.description: When the task's latest successful run that served a fact_time_reached time (SCH-M CF-1) or a fact probe's unknown period (SS-5) was dispatched, in Unix milliseconds.

table_column.description: The name of a column of a standard-pack table (Workflow #357 DB-1, M-357a v1.1 section 6.1).

table_id.description: The id of a standard-pack table, its file name without .json (Workflow #357 DB-2, M-357a v1.1 section 6.1).

table_mismatch.description: How a standard-pack table differs from the selection document's declaration of it (Workflow #357 DB-2, M-357a v1.1 section 6.1).

plan_id.description: An installer plan's id, plan-<16 hex> (contracts/install-cli.md).

install_refusal.description: Why an installer command refused, or failed without leaving an unfinished operation.

release_checks.description: The failed checks of a release folder.

rollback_gate_parts.description: The failed parts of the rollback gate.

install_guards.description: The installer guards that failed or could not be evaluated.

install_caveat.description: What an installer command noted while its work went on: something left unchecked, pending or on the previous build.

attempt_phase.description: Why another attempt of an installer operation cannot run now: running or handover (install-cli.md; design 3.11, v4.1; the install phase keeps the key phase).

hold_reason.description: The deployment pause reason a form was computed for (install-cli.md, "Forms"; design 3.1, v4.1), or (Workflow #434 LAB-3 fix 1) the hold's reason a refusal hold_not_owned names.

s0_from.description: The installer operation whose S0 a start's post-start checks will judge against, null when none counts (design 3.15, v4.1).

player_hold_range.description: The player-hold range [min, max] of the Runtime a player_holds guard judged (design 3.10).

confirm_argv.description: The argv after the program name that confirms the UI half (design 3.15, confirm_ui_running).

child_pid.description: The process id of a fixed entry's child (stable-entry.md).

child_state.description: Whether a graphical entry's child still ran when the entry exited (stable-entry.md).

child_exit_code.description: The exit code of a fixed entry's child that exited (stable-entry.md).

inherited_sha256.description: The SHA-256 of an inherited install selection (stable-entry.md).

active_sha256.description: The SHA-256 of install\active.json as read (stable-entry.md; install-cli.md).

install_member.description: A member of an install selection: runtime, tools or ui (design 2.3).

idle_action.description: An instance's idle action (IDLE-1): close_app or stop_emulator, as idle.action spells it. IDLE-2: auto in an instance_idle_action_unsupported of the action in effect; return_home for a rest at home, the tier auto takes first (never a value of idle.action); every other record names the tier taken, never auto.

display_problem.description: Why the display adapter cannot map a frame, a region or an input box (Workflow #392 DA-1, model 392 v1.2 §9.1).

frame_width.description: The width of a delivered frame, device-frame pixels (Workflow #392 DA-1).

frame_height.description: The height of a delivered frame, device-frame pixels (Workflow #392 DA-1).

base_width.description: The width of a task package's base coordinate space (its coordinate_space), pixels (Workflow #392 DA-1).

base_height.description: The height of a task package's base coordinate space (its coordinate_space), pixels (Workflow #392 DA-1).

memory_priority_requested.description: The memory priority actingd asked the operating system for its own process at start, Windows' MEMORY_PRIORITY level: 5 for host.process_memory_priority normal, 2 for low (RB-2).

memory_priority_read.description: The memory priority of actingd's own process as the operating system reported it after the start set it, Windows' MEMORY_PRIORITY level (RB-2).

io_priority_requested.description: The I/O priority hint actingd asked the operating system for its own process at start, Windows' IO_PRIORITY_HINT: 2 for host.process_io_priority normal, 1 for low (RB-2).

io_priority_read.description: The I/O priority hint of actingd's own process as the operating system reported it after the start set it, Windows' IO_PRIORITY_HINT (RB-2).

policy_input.description: Which input of a policy evaluation a check refused: a fact, a settled run's outcome, a pair's task state, its completed activity window, a pool reading or a priority offset (ISO-PE, #419).

policy_input_problem.description: Why a check refused a policy evaluation input (ISO-PE, #419).

observed_at_unix_ms.description: When a refused input was observed, in Unix milliseconds (ISO-PE, #419).

evaluated_at_unix_ms.description: The time of the policy evaluation that refused an input, in Unix milliseconds (ISO-PE, #419).

benefit_gap.description: Why a judged candidate's net benefit is unknown: no declared effect, a pending entry, a pending or missing valuation of a pool it touches, or an unknown reading of a regenerating pool it consumes (SS-2b, contracts/scheduling/README.md "Net benefit within a tier").

benefit_milli.description: A judged candidate's net benefit B in milli: the value of what one run produces less the cost of what it consumes, each at the resource layer's weight per valuation step (SS-2b; SS-2h: a consumption at its full weight whatever the pool's fill, and for the head of a capped spending order the part of its consumption above the stop line free).

expected_duration_ms.description: The expected duration E a judged candidate's net benefit is divided by to rank it: the pair's expected duration, else its last settled run's, else the declared one, in milliseconds (SS-2b).

action_gap_ms.description: The gap a step drew between its recognition and its input under execution.action_gap.kind random, in milliseconds (ACT-2).

loading_event.description: What a frame of a wait did with the package's loading pages: the first transition frame of a stretch, the first frame after one, or a transition frame past the wait's allowance (Workflow #407 LOAD-3, since 0.12.37).

loading_page_id.description: The loading page a transition frame showed: the first of the wait's loading pages that held on it, in their order, or the page of the package the confirmation adds as one (Workflow #407 LOAD-3, since 0.12.37).

loading_ms.description: The budget time the transition frames of one input's waits had spent of their allowance, in milliseconds: before the frame for entered, up to the frame for left and limit_reached (Workflow #407 LOAD-3, since 0.12.37).

loading_limit_ms.description: The allowance of one input's waits for transition frames in effect, in milliseconds of budget time: the operation's loading.max_ms, else its wait page's max_ms, else the package's (Workflow #407 LOAD-3, since 0.12.37).

loading_exit_gap_ms.description: The budget time between the last transition frame of a stretch and the first frame after it, in milliseconds: how late the wait saw the loading end, which the back-off over transition frames lengthens (Workflow #407 LOAD-3, since 0.12.37).

reading_value.description: A fact reading as the admission of a dispatch read it, its canonical JSON ({"type": <kind>, "value": <value>}), at most 128 bytes (SS-4, contracts/scheduling/README.md "No-progress guard").

reading_digest.description: The SHA-256 of a fact reading's canonical JSON, in place of reading_value when that is longer than 128 bytes (SS-4).

basis_readings.description: The basis of a held pair's latest dispatch, one record per fact its admission read, ordered by scope and key, at most 32: the key and the reading the admission read (reading_value or reading_digest, and observed_at_unix_ms when it was observed), none when the key had no reading (SS-4).

hold_id.description: A player hold's identity: the request_id of the AcquirePlayerHold that set it (Workflow #429 R-7a).

hold_phase.description: A player hold's phase: the hold now, or the one a refusal names (R-7a).

failed_phase.description: The phase a player hold operation failed in (R-7a).

hold_revision.description: An instance's player hold slot revision: the hold's, or the slot's after a release (R-7a).

current_owner_epoch.description: The owner epoch now, in a refused player hold expectation (R-7a).

current_hold_id.description: The hold now, in a refused player hold expectation (R-7a).

current_revision.description: The hold slot revision now, in a refused player hold expectation (R-7a).

current_phase.description: The hold's phase now, in a refused player hold expectation (R-7a).

hold_count.description: How many persisted player holds of registered instances a start found (R-7a).

restored_from_phase.description: Whether a restored player hold had finished its hand-back before the stop (R-7a).

operation_kind.description: The kind of the player hold request a settlement judged (R-7a).

settlement_rule.description: The row of the player hold settlement table that decided (R-7a).

settlement_trigger.description: Why the client settled a player hold request from Status: dropped, timed_out or reopened (R-7a).

settlement_final.description: Whether reading Status again can no longer change a player hold settlement (R-7a).

settlement_outcome.description: What a settled player hold request did (R-7a; the design's outcome, renamed because outcome names the envelope).

settlement_observed.description: What an unconfirmed player hold settlement saw (R-7a).

hold_next.description: What a release of a player hold did next (R-7a).

startup_package.description: What a release of a player hold did with the startup package (R-7a).

startup_package_withheld.description: The pause that holds the startup package a release queued (R-7a; its two values are the two pauses of player_hold_next).

pause_instance_revision.description: The revision of the instance pause in effect when a player hold ended (R-7a).

pause_global_revision.description: The revision of the global pause in effect when a player hold ended (R-7a).

drained_finished.description: The in-flight runs a player hold's drain let finish (R-7a).

drained_cancelled.description: The in-flight runs a player hold's drain stopped at a checkpoint (R-7a).

selfcheck_failure_code.description: The failure_code of a release's reconnect self-check (R-7a).

hold_restored.description: A settlement found the player hold restored from its persisted row (R-7a, rows A11 and A12).

source_actor.description: Who set the player hold: the envelope's actor (R-7a).

source_channel.description: The channel the player hold was set on (R-7a).

source_via.description: The counter that forwarded the Lab request that set the player hold (R-7a; a ChannelVia value).

ended_by_actor.description: Who ended, or is ending, the player hold (R-7a).

ended_by_channel.description: The channel the player hold was ended on (R-7a).

ended_by_via.description: The counter that forwarded the Lab request that ended the player hold (R-7a).

ended_by_state.description: The state of the release that ended the player hold (R-7a).

operation_kind_now.description: The kind of the instance's player hold record now (R-7a).

operation_state_now.description: The state of the instance's player hold record now (R-7a).

tolerance_milli.description: The rounding bound ε of a judged candidate's exact net benefit S, rounded up to a whole milli: the sum over the pools it produces of R/(2000·Q) + n·(2W+1)/(4000·Q) and over the pools it consumes of C/(2000·Q) + m·(2W+1)/(4000·Q), with R and C its per-run production and consumption in thousandths, n and m the pool's expected_amount_milli entries, W the pool's weight and Q its valuation scale (SS-2d, contracts/scheduling/README.md "Within tolerance"; SS-2h: the whole consumption, the regenerating share σ retired with SS-2b's discount).

zero_tier.description: What became of a judged candidate whose exact net benefit is within its rounding bound (|S| ≤ ε): released into the last place of its tier, or deferred because its task is not marked benefit_realization, no pool it produces is weighed above 0 on its instance, or its latest run there failed (SS-2d).

current_version.description: The edit-version token now of what a refused request's expected_version named (fact_observation_version_conflict; Workflow #429 R-4, since 0.12.36): opaque and compared only for equality, the expected_version to send next; a denied receipt keeps it in codes mode.

resume_after_sequence.description: The ledger sequence after which an event subscription that ended resumes: the after_sequence of the cursor to subscribe again with, every event at or before it having reached its client or been filtered out (subscription_lagged; #419 SUB-LAG-1, since 0.12.37); a failed receipt keeps it in codes mode.

pool_capacity.description: The capacity a pool's reading was held to at the evaluation, in the pool's real units: a constant capacity, or the one read from its fact (SS-2h, contracts/scheduling/README.md "Pool lines").

stop_line.description: A pool's stop line at the evaluation, in the pool's real units: the capped spending order spends the pool down to it; without lines the capacity (SS-2h, contracts/scheduling/README.md "Pool lines").

hard_line.description: A pool's hard line at the evaluation, in the pool's real units: no dispatch the scheduler chooses leaves the pool below it; without lines 0 (SS-2h, contracts/scheduling/README.md "Pool lines").

pool_reading.description: A pool's reading the lines were checked against, in the pool's real units: its projected amount less the consumption its reading does not show yet; negative when that consumption exceeds the amount (SS-2h).

capped_episode.description: Which capped episode of the pool on the instance, counted from 1 since the Runtime started: an episode begins when the reading reaches the cap (SS-2h, contracts/scheduling/README.md "Capped spending order"); since SCHED-C1d (0.12.53) an episode a start keeps (host.capped_episodes) keeps its number, and the next one counts on from it.

capped_round.description: Which round of the capped episode, from 1: the first round takes limited tasks too, every later one only repeatable tasks (SS-2h).

capped_rank.description: A dispatch's place, from 1, in its round's frozen order of the pool's consumers by value per unit consumed (SS-2h).

pool_line_hold.description: Why a pool's lines hold a judged candidate back this round (SS-2h, contracts/scheduling/README.md "Pool lines", "Capped spending order").

warning_code.description: The code of a warning a record lists, for example a compile warning of a composed catalog (#428 CW-1).

compile_warnings.description: The compile warnings of the composed catalog the scheduler workbench activated that the game's schedule.json gave: each warning's code and its JSON pointer in that file, each place once, in code then pointer order (#428 CW-1, contracts/standard-pack-schedule.md "The scheduler workbench").

fact_keys.description: The record-list fact keys a list maximum read, in the order of its lists, at most 16 (Workflow #428 S168-5a, contracts/selection-policy.md "Table maximum over a list").

maximum.description: The largest value a list maximum read: the largest integer of its table column over the listed keys of the pinned class (Workflow #428 S168-5a).

maximum_identity.description: The smallest listed key, in byte order, whose row holds a list maximum's largest value: a business identity, never screen text (Workflow #428 S168-5a).

bound.description: Whether a list maximum that names a lower_bound_column read an exact value or a lower bound: exact when every listed key of the pinned class has a value, at_least when a key has none (Workflow #428 S168-LB1b, contracts/selection-policy.md "Lower bound of a list maximum").

unknown_count.description: The listed keys a list maximum read with no value: a key with no row in the table, or with a null value cell of the pinned class (Workflow #428 S168-LB1b).

lower_bound.description: The lower bound L a list maximum read as at least: the largest of the known values and of the bounds the table gives the keys without a value (Workflow #428 S168-LB1b).

lower_bound_identity.description: The smallest listed key, in byte order, that gives a list maximum's lower bound L, by its value or by its bound: a business identity, never screen text (Workflow #428 S168-LB1b).

fixed_value_milli.description: A task's fixed value V in milli of its game's value unit: the value of one run without the cost of the pools it consumes, written in its standard pack (the schedule.json rule member fixed_value_milli, the catalog's benefit_fixed_value_milli); a judged candidate's net benefit is V less the cost of what it consumes (#428 SCHED-C1a, contracts/scheduling/README.md "Fixed values written in the pack").

run_origin.description: Who started the run a StopInstanceRun refused: the Runtime itself (a startup package, a ladder rung, an idle action's rest), the one origin it refuses since 0.12.55 (Workflow #429 R-6b2), when it stops a policy run; 0.12.53 also refused a policy run with policy. Kept in codes mode (Workflow #429 R-6).

trigger_line.description: A pool's trigger line at the evaluation, in the pool's real units, when the pool writes one: a capped episode begins at a reading at or above it; without one the capacity (#428 SCHED-C1c, contracts/scheduling/README.md "Pool lines", "The trigger line").

least_consumption.description: The least consumption of one run, in whole units of the pool, among a pool's judged consumers on an instance, by their declared consumption (#428 SCHED-C1c, contracts/scheduling/README.md "A pool its lines cannot spend").

lines_source.description: Where the lines of a pool in effect on an instance come from: the instance's own instance.<instance id>.scheduling.pool_lines, the catalog's lines, or the defaults (#428 SCHED-C1e, contracts/scheduling/README.md "Lines for one instance").

consumption.description: One run's consumption of a pool by a task in an evaluation, in whole units of the pool (the ⌈C/1000⌉ the decision reads), when the task's consumption of the pool is read from a fact: the fact's usable value, or the entry's fallback (#428 SCHED-C1f1, contracts/scheduling/README.md "A run's consumption read from a fact").

consumption_source.description: Where the amount of a task's consumption of a pool read from a fact comes from in an evaluation: the fact's usable record of the instance, or the entry's fallback (#428 SCHED-C1f1, contracts/scheduling/README.md "A run's consumption read from a fact").

state_problem.description: Which kind of invalid state contained_task_state_invalid ended a contained task's run with (#428 DIAG-SI, since 0.12.55).

phase_id.description: The declared id of a stage of a phased route (a task's phases[].id): the stage the run was in (#428 DIAG-SI, since 0.12.55).

held_state.description: How a held pair stood when task_held reported it: the not-run explanation row's eligibility (Workflow #438 HELD-1, since 0.12.56). Kept in codes mode.

held_end.description: How a hold that task_held reported ended, the value of task_held_ended (Workflow #438 HELD-1, since 0.12.56). Kept in codes mode.

held_since_unix_ms.description: The start of a hold: the not-run explanation row's since_unix_ms, the first evaluation of the run of evaluations in which the pair kept its why code (Workflow #438 HELD-1, since 0.12.56).

held_for_ms.description: How long a pair has been held: the evaluation time less held_since_unix_ms, at the held record or at the evaluation that found the hold ended (Workflow #438 HELD-1, since 0.12.56).

held_after_ms.description: The threshold in effect for the instance when a held record was written, scheduling.task_held.after_ms (Workflow #438 HELD-1, since 0.12.56).

device_group_problem.description: Which rule of device groups the instances[] entries that share one device break (Workflow #437 MAPP-1, since 0.12.56).

device_group_wait.description: Why a member of a device group waits for its device: what another member of the device does (Workflow #437 MAPP-1, since 0.12.56).

application_switch_step.description: Which step of the switch that brings a member of a device group to the front before its run failed (Workflow #437 MAPP-2a, since 0.12.59).

variable_name.description: A variable a package's control.json declares, the last segment of the key session.dispatch.parameter.<name> a run reads it under (Workflow #463 V2, since 0.12.61).

value_json.description: The value a run reads of a variable, as compact JSON: an option value in quotes, a whole number, true or false, or a list of option values; at most 1024 bytes, the longest value text the goal store keeps for an entry (Workflow #463 V2, since 0.12.61; a json key since its fix round 1).

variable_source.description: Where the value a policy run reads of a variable comes from: the value set on the application, or the package's default (Workflow #463 V2, since 0.12.61).

set_unix_ms.description: When the value an application holds for a variable was set: its entry row's set_unix_ms in the session.resource_targets v3 record (Workflow #463 V2, since 0.12.61).

set_channel.description: The channel of the connection that set the value an application holds for a variable: its entry row's channel (Workflow #463 V2, since 0.12.61).

variable_problem.description: Why the value set on an application for a variable was not handed to a run, which reads the package's default; or keys_left_out, an ordered value handed to the run in part (Workflow #463 V2, since 0.12.61).

value_sha256.description: The sha256 of the text of a variable's value (its compact JSON) whose text the ledger record of a dispatch's reason left out, because the reason would pass an outcome record's bound (Workflow #463 V2 fix round 2, since 0.12.61).

value_bytes.description: The length in bytes of the text of a variable's value whose text the ledger record of a dispatch's reason left out (Workflow #463 V2 fix round 2, since 0.12.61).

value_json_left_out.description: true: the record carries value_sha256 and value_bytes in place of value_json, because the reason would pass an outcome record's bound; the run read the value whole from the reason chain it was admitted with (Workflow #463 V2 fix round 2, since 0.12.61).

variable_values.description: The values a policy dispatch hands its run for the variables its package declares, one record each in declaration order: the name, where the value comes from, the value (absent only for a default longer than 1024 bytes, which the run reads from its package), when and through which channel the application's value was set when it holds one and both can be read, and why that value was not applied when it was not, or keys_left_out when it was applied in part (Workflow #463 V2, since 0.12.61). Fix round 2: in the ledger record, a value whose text would make the reason pass an outcome record's bound (32 KiB less the envelope's own room) carries value_sha256, value_bytes and value_json_left_out in place of value_json, the longest first until the reason fits; the run reads every value whole from the reason chain it was admitted with.

declaration_sha256.description: The sha256 of a variable's declaration as its control.json writes it, in compact JSON (Workflow #463 V2, since 0.12.61).

goals_failure.description: Why a game root's goals.json is not applied while the root runs: the reader refused it, or it could not be read (Workflow #463 V2 fix round 2, since 0.12.61).

goal_name.description: The name an EditGoal named: an entry of the application's goals.json, a variable a package declares, or an other resource target's id; absent when the request's name has no entry name's form (Workflow #463 V3, since 0.12.61).

goal_problem.description: Why an EditGoal was refused under the fact write gate, after the version comparison (Workflow #463 V3, since 0.12.61).

adopt_problem.description: Which check of actinglab standard-pack adopt refused (Workflow #464 P1, since 0.12.61).

readiness_item.description: Which of the thirteen readiness items of a pack waits or was not judged: S1 to S7 of the game root, I1 to I6 of an installation (Workflow #464 P3, since 0.12.61).

readiness_problem.description: Why a readiness item keeps a pack from being dispatched (Workflow #464 P3, since 0.12.61).

readiness_unjudged.description: Why a readiness item of a pack was not judged, or the information line of item I3 (Workflow #464 P3, since 0.12.61).

required_revision.description: The interface revision a content declares or needs: the package maximum a bundle declares, beside range_min and range_max of the range that does not hold it (Workflow #464 P3, since 0.12.61).

blocking_package_id.description: The package whose problem keeps another pack waiting: the pack of a follower's head (head_waiting), the layer a prerequisite chain was refused at (prerequisite_unregistered, prerequisite_refused), the return-home package the Runtime's entry would refuse for a page-graph pack's home entry (return_home_refused, fix round 2), the pack standard-pack check refused the root at (root_refused) (Workflow #464 P3 fix round 1, since 0.12.61).

report_part.description: Which part of a problem report could not be read (Workflow #467 RPT-1, since 0.12.61).

report_part_reason.description: Why a part of a problem report is missing (Workflow #467 RPT-1, since 0.12.61).

report_write_step.description: The step of writing a problem report that failed (Workflow #467 RPT-1, since 0.12.61).

report_fit.description: Whether a problem report fits its size bound after the parts the bound may leave out were left out (Workflow #467 RPT-1, since 0.12.61).

report_output_root.description: The root a refused output directory of a problem report lies in (Workflow #467 RPT-1, since 0.12.61).

confirmation_problem.description: What the program saw where the confirmation of the page a step awaits ended, or the declared error page a run stood on: one word per situation it tells apart there, beside the code and never in its detail text (Workflow #469 V0, since 0.12.62).

guard_problem.description: Why an operation's guard refused its input (Workflow #469 V0, since 0.12.62).

availability_source.description: Who withdrew an application's availability, read from the source of the active session.instance.available record that withdrew it (Workflow #469 V0, since 0.12.62).

pause_cause.description: Why a failure paused its task on the application, in the settlement's own order (Workflow #469 V0, since 0.12.62).

break_in_problem.description: What of a scheduled run's break-in could not be established before the run executed: the package's content or the pair's break-in record (Workflow #463 U1b fix round 3, since 0.12.63).

trial_state_place.description: Where a state directory refused for trial records lies: a repository or an installed root (Workflow #463 S3-10, since 0.12.64).

trial_record_problem.description: Why a file of a trial record's name is not read as that record: the read failed, it is too large, it does not decode, or it is not the record its name says (Workflow #463 S3-10 fix round 2, since 0.12.64).

trial_collect_problem.description: Why the run a trial's --collect names is not a trial's run: its facts do not name the trial's package or the instance the trial is for, or (fix round 2) do not show a run sent by hand on the Lab's channel (Workflow #463 S3-11, since 0.12.65).

drop_problem.description: Why record mark's drop_step does not drop a step before the last of a Lab recording: the stored frames do not hold what the comparison needs, or they show a change at its press (#463 S2-7, since 0.12.68; fix round 1: the tool refuses only what the stored frames contradict, whether the press mattered is the agent's judgement).

drop_comparison.description: Which of the two comparisons of two stored frames showed the change for which record mark's drop_step refuses a step before the last (record_drop_unproven with drop_problem screen_changed or next_screen_differs): the whole frame or the neighbourhood of the press (#463 S2-7 fix round 1, since 0.12.68).

regression_problem.description: The word of the first failed check of a regression case record stop made from a recording for the package it generated, which misses on that package (record_case_failed; #463 S2-10, since 0.12.70); every failed check of the case is in the refusal's details.

scan_problem.description: Why the swipes recorded before a press of a Lab recording cannot be folded into one scrolling search of that press, the fold undone, a step of the fold acted on, or the fold generated (record_scan_invalid; #463 S2-8', since 0.12.70).

key_problem.description: Why a Lab recording step's key, the back key a step presses in place of a click, declared after the fact and never sent while recording, cannot be declared or generated (record_key_invalid; #463 KR-1, since 0.12.70).

privacy_rect_kind.description: Which rectangle of a package a privacy finding names: the kind of a region a recognition target of the package reads, or a rectangle of a regression case's scene (#463 PRIV-1, contracts/privacy-zones.md, since 0.12.74; declared ahead of the first answer of the privacy_ codes).

privacy_zone_id.description: The id of a sensitive zone of a repository root's privacy-zones.json, unique within its base size (#463 PRIV-1, since 0.12.74).

privacy_zone_kind.description: What a sensitive zone holds, its kind in privacy-zones.json: identity (nothing may read there) or value (only a reading may read there, and no scene may hold its pixels) (#463 PRIV-1 amendment 1, the owner's ruling of 11-18, since 0.12.74).

privacy_reading.description: Whether the region of a privacy finding is a reading: a region the kernel reads as a number at run time, whether or not the number is published as a fact (a mark's target, an adjustment's amount, a candidate layout's integer feature, ocr_integer, a select's quantity column among them, an integer field of the entry task's OCR fields, in a field list or not, a value test's sides), or a layout's shared read that gives its text to one; a rectangle of a case's scene is never one (#463 PRIV-1 amendment 1 and fix rounds 1 and 2, contracts/privacy-zones.md "A reading", since 0.12.74).

privacy_unseen_kind.description: What a rectangle check of a package cannot see: a text an OCR target expects, an alias a candidate layout's identity entry is read as, a regression case of another schema (#463 PRIV-1, since 0.12.74).

privacy_unseen_counts.description: What a rectangle check of a package cannot see, each kind with its count, in the vocabulary's order (#463 PRIV-1, contracts/privacy-zones.md "What a rectangle cannot see", since 0.12.74).

idle_wake_cause.description: Why an idle instance's wake was queued, on instance_idle_action with operation queue_idle_wake: a task of the instance due that can be dispatched now (with task_id), the idle action in effect changed, a wake the start owed, or the planned wake time reached (#484 IDLE-W2, contracts/runtime-config.md "What wakes an idle instance", since 0.12.75).

cause_relation.description: How a link relates to the outcome it is attached to.

caused_by.description: The link caused the outcome (the default).

cleanup.description: A cleanup step that ran after the outcome and failed or left something behind.

secondary.description: A second failure while recovering from the outcome.

recording.description: A failure while recording the outcome.

related.description: A related result, for example a relayed conclusion.

after_commit.description: A failure after the main transaction committed.

note.description: A note the operation tolerated, for example a check-config warning.

capture_frame_context.description: The capture frame context of an observation.

close_unlock_ledger.description: Closing the ledger after an owner unlock.

committed_planning_fact.description: A planning fact that was already committed.

prior_epoch_startup_cleanup.description: Startup cleanup of an earlier owner epoch.

selection_record_ledger.description: Writing a selection record to the ledger.

side_file_cleanup.description: Cleanup of an owner journal side file.

raw_source.description: The third party whose text raw_text carries.

os.description: The operating system or file system.

io_kind.description: The Rust io::ErrorKind of an I/O failure, in snake_case.

uncategorized.description: An io::ErrorKind this vocabulary does not list; os_error and raw_text tell more.

origin_module.description: The Runtime module that produced a result.

event_action.description: The action a ledger record belongs to.

device.backend_switched.description: An instance's touch and capture backends switched (#402 HS-2).

policy_failure_class.description: The class of a policy failure.

policy_failure_disposition.description: What policy does after a failure.

unknown_reason.description: Why an input a selection document reads could not be read as a known value.

fact_missing.description: No record exists under the fact key.

fact_expired.description: The record's own expiry has passed.

fact_stale.description: The record is older than the freshness bound the document declares.

fact_low_confidence.description: The record's confidence is below the floor the document declares.

fact_not_scalar.description: The record holds an artifact or a record list, not a scalar.

type_mismatch.description: The value present does not have the declared type.

field_missing.description: The candidate carries no value under the field name.

resource_observation_missing.description: No observation exists for the resource a rule reads.

lookup_miss.description: No lookup entry covers the value and the transform declares no default.

dependency_state_missing.description: No terminal state is recorded for the task a predicate depends on.

outcome_missing.description: No result is recorded under the task's outcome key.

outcome_expired.description: The result recorded under the task's outcome key has expired.

resource_outcome_missing.description: No result is recorded for the resource a pool reads from a task's outcome.

unknown_clause.description: An on_unknown clause of a selection document that the scheduling layer does not apply.

drop_candidate.description: The clause drops the candidate from ranking.

substitute.description: The clause substitutes a declared verdict (gate) or value (term).

reader_problem.description: Why no reader can refresh an instance fact, or what is wrong with a reader binding.

key_not_marked.description: The recognition maintenance package carries no reading mark for the key.

designated_operation.description: The package declares a designated operation, so it is not a reader.

no_marks.description: The package carries no reading mark.

recognize_only.description: The package is recognize-only, so it is not a reader.

stability_termination.description: The package ends on a stability termination, so it is not a reader.

policy_fact_authority.description: The key is a policy fact of the catalog, so a reading of it is refused.

live_pool_key.description: The key is observed by a ledger-fact pool, so a reading of it was refused. No longer given since Workflow #390 POOL-1: such a reading is the pool's base.

package_unbound.description: The instance has no recognition maintenance package bound.

not_declared.description: The bound package is not declared for recognition maintenance, so the binding is ignored.

disabled.description: Fact refresh is turned off in the configuration.

confidence_below_document.description: The reading mark's confidence floor is below the floor the document declares.

interval_exceeds_freshness.description: The minimum reading interval exceeds the freshness the document or the mark requires.

package_unreadable.description: The bound package cannot be read or admitted (Workflow #384 D2-S2).

reading_problem.description: Why a reading mark gave no reading on a frame handed to recognition (Workflow #384 D2-S2).

invalid_integer.description: The text is not an integer of the declared format.

overflow.description: The integer does not fit 64 bits.

out_of_range.description: The integer is outside the declared range.

region_unresolved.description: The OCR target's region could not be placed on the frame.

provider_failed.description: The OCR provider failed, or the recognition ended without an answer.

low_confidence.description: The confidence is below the mark's floor.

join_timeout.description: The recognition had not returned when the run's join timeout ended.

no_agreement.description: The frames of the mark's agreement did not all read the same value (Workflow #411 B1); the mark writes no fact.

list_position_unread.description: Workflow #428 S168-4: a position of a read_list step's list was readable at least once but holds no fixed Known reading of its identity or of a column's feature; the list writes nothing. Workflow #450 FL-1b: a frame of a field list whose key or a column is not resolved at the list's minimum_confidence_milli (frame_indices names those frames); the list writes nothing.

list_duplicate_key.description: Workflow #428 S168-4: two positions of a read_list step's list read the same business ID; the list writes nothing. Workflow #450 FL-1b: a field list read one key on two frames or more, adjacent or not, with equal or different columns; the core never folds, sums or picks one (frame_indices names every frame that holds a repeated key); the list writes nothing.

list_rows_exceeded.description: Workflow #428 S168-4: a read_list step's list showed more positions than one fact holds; the scan stopped there and the list writes nothing. Since 0.12.55 (Workflow #428 S168-LB1a) a fact holds 1024 rows, so at the 1025th position; before it, 256, at the 257th.

list_bytes_exceeded.description: Workflow #428 S168-LB1a (since 0.12.55): a read_list step's list was read whole, within the row bound, but its record is larger than one observation holds (512 KiB); nothing is cut to fit, the list writes nothing and the key's earlier record stays.

list_start_unseen.description: Workflow #450 FL-1b (since 0.12.59): a field list's first frame did not meet its start (a page, a required target, a forbidden target), so the run may have begun inside the list; count is the frames collected and frame_indices the first frame. The list writes nothing and the key's earlier record stays.

list_end_unseen.description: Workflow #450 FL-1b (since 0.12.59): a successful run collected frames of a field list and none met its end (the end page was not reached, not collected past max_frames, or its targets did not hold); count is the frames collected and frame_indices the last frame. The list writes nothing and the key's earlier record stays.

scan_alignment_failure.description: Why a scan session found no single shift for a frame (Workflow #308 SEL-L3).

too_few_matches.description: No cluster of pairs reaches min_overlap_instances.

no_consistent_shift.description: No cluster of pairs is consistent, for any other reason.

ambiguous_shift.description: Two or more consistent clusters lie inside the motion's window.

unexpected_displacement.description: No consistent cluster lies inside the motion's window, but one lies outside it.

scan_spacing_failure.description: Which spacing check of a scan session found a missed anchor (Workflow #308 SEL-L3).

axis_gap.description: Two consecutive rows lie further apart than max_axis_gap_px.

row_short.description: A row holds another number of positions than spacing.columns.

leading_gap.description: The first row starts further from the band's leading edge than max_axis_gap_px.

trailing_gap.description: The last row starts further from the band's trailing edge than max_trailing_gap_px.

cross_gap.description: A row's first position, or the next one, lies further across the axis than max_cross_lead_px or max_cross_gap_px.

scan_bound.description: Which bound of a scan session ran out (Workflow #308 SEL-L3).

reposition_viewports.description: max_reposition_viewports: the rewind and return viewports.

duration.description: max_ms, or the task's own deadline when it comes first.

selection_kind.description: The kind of a selection policy's decision (Workflow #308).

empty.description: No candidate survived and the mode accepts an empty answer.

insufficient.description: Fewer candidates survived than the policy requires.

ambiguous.description: Candidates tied at the cut after every tie-break key.

unknown.description: The evaluation aborted on an unusable input.

selection_blocking.description: Why unknown instances keep a selection decision from standing (Workflow #308 SEL-L4b).

unknown_instances.description: An empty or insufficient decision with at least one unknown instance.

outranked_possible.description: A selected decision that an unknown instance might outrank.

identity_state.description: How a confirmed or expected business identity differed from the chosen one (Workflow #308 SEL-L4b).

absent.description: No actionable instance at the chosen position or, for a template expect_identity, no pool entry passed.

unknown.description: Only Unknown readings until the timeout.

no_choice.description: The choice_of step chose nothing in this run.

selection_confirm.description: How a select step confirms its choice on its confirmation frame, as its select.confirm declares it (Workflow #404 FS-3).

track.description: The confirmation frame is decided again and its choice stands when its anchor match origin lies within the step's track_px of the evaluated choice's.

list_max_bound.description: How a list maximum that names a lower_bound_column read (Workflow #428 S168-LB1b, contracts/selection-policy.md "Lower bound of a list maximum").

exact.description: Every listed key of the pinned class has a value: the read is the largest value M, or the document's empty when no listed key is of the class.

at_least.description: A listed key has no value (no row, or a null value cell of the class) and a value or a bound is known: the read is every value from L up.

adjustment_reason.description: Why a run's confirmed resource adjustment wrote nothing (Workflow #384 D2-S3).

base_missing.description: The key had no current record to adjust.

base_expired.description: The key's current record had expired.

newer_observation.description: An observation of the key at or after the confirmation already holds the change.

amount_unresolved.description: The change the screen shows could not be read; the key's record is dropped.

after_read_missing.description: No reading of the key followed the confirmation; the key's record is dropped.

benefit_gap.description: Why a judged candidate's net benefit is unknown, the value of benefit_unknown (SS-2b, contracts/scheduling/README.md "Net benefit within a tier"). Unknown is never 0: the known part is never added up.

no_effects.description: The task declares no produces and no consumes entry.

entry_pending.description: An entry's amount is the pending marker; pool_id names its pool.

valuation_pending.description: A pool the task touches has the pending marker for its valuation; pool_id names it.

valuation_missing.description: A pool the task touches has no valuation for the instance; pool_id names it.

reading_unknown.description: A regenerating pool the task consumes has a reading that is unknown or expired; pool_id names the pool, fact_key and unknown_reason its reading when it reads a fact, and the fact refresh is asked for it.

loading_event.description: What a frame of a wait did with the package's loading pages, the value of contained_task_loading_recorded (Workflow #407 LOAD-3, since 0.12.37; contracts/resource-declarations.md "Loading pages").

entered.description: The first transition frame of a stretch of them: a loading page held, row 3 of the frame judgement. page_id is the page of the package it suppresses, when one held.

left.description: The first frame after a stretch of transition frames that is none. page_id is the page that held on it (a destination, another page, or none); loading_exit_gap_ms is the time since the stretch's last transition frame.

limit_reached.description: A transition frame after the input's allowance was spent: under on the wait ends on it with its own code and the loading values; under shadow it is recorded once and nothing changes.

zero_tier.description: What became of a judged candidate within its rounding bound, the value of benefit_within_tolerance (SS-2d, contracts/scheduling/README.md "Within tolerance"). Its sign is not trusted: only a model-verified realization task may run, last in its tier.

released.description: Its task is marked benefit_realization, its B is known, a pool it produces is weighed above 0 on its instance and its latest run there did not fail: it takes part in the allocation after every unjudged and every positive judged candidate of the business tier, every later gate applying.

unmarked.description: Its task is not marked benefit_realization: deferred.

no_downstream_value.description: No pool it produces is weighed above 0 on its instance (neither a model price nor a goal gives it a use): deferred.

latest_failed.description: Its latest run on the instance failed: deferred; the failure keeps its own retry and escalation path, the zero tier does not retry it.

pool_line_hold.description: Why a pool's lines hold a judged candidate back, the value of pool_line_held (SS-2h, contracts/scheduling/README.md "Pool lines", "Capped spending order"). The lines constrain the scheduler only: manual requests and the Runtime's own tasks are not held.

would_cross_hard_line.description: Below the cap: its run would leave the pool below its hard line (amount_after, hard_line).

capped_not_dispatchable.description: Capped: it was no candidate when its round's order was frozen, or is none now (gate_code its own reason, when registered), or a later gate of its own (the reserve gate, a budget, a window, a package hold or a remedy round of the Runtime's admission) refused it in the round, which passed it (gate_code that gate's code); it is listed again at the next round.

capped_limited_spent.description: Capped, from an episode's second round on: its task is marked benefit_limited, so only the first round takes it; the next episode's first round takes it again.

capped_would_cross_hard_line.description: Capped: its run, from the reading the round accumulates to it, would leave the pool below its hard line (amount_after), so the round skips it and tries the next.

capped_round_empty.description: Capped: the round lists no task (none can be dispatched now, none fits above the hard line, or from the second round none is repeatable), so the episode ends.

capped_not_head.description: Capped: another consumer of the pool is the head of the round's order (task_id), or this one already ran in the round; one consumer of the pool is dispatched at a time.

capped_cap_unknown.description: The pool's capacity, its reading or a fact a line reads gives no value (fact_key and unknown_reason when a fact gives none), so its written lines cannot be kept and it enters no capped state; since SCHED-C1d (0.12.53) an episode under way waits instead of ending, its consumers held with this token whether or not the pool writes lines, and goes on, or ends by its rule, once the values come back.

lines_invalid.description: The lines read at the evaluation break their rules: the stop line not above the hard line, or a line above the capacity or below 0 (stop_line, hard_line, pool_capacity).

lines_source.description: Where the lines of a pool in effect on an instance come from, a value of pool_line_held (on each hold that carries the lines), capped_spend and pool_lines_unspendable (#428 SCHED-C1e, contracts/scheduling/README.md "Lines for one instance"). An instance's set replaces the catalog's lines of the pool whole; the catalog's lines stay every other instance's.

instance.description: The instance's own instance.<instance id>.scheduling.pool_lines names the pool: its stop line, hard line and trigger line (the capacity when the set writes none, not the catalog's).

catalog.description: The catalog's lines of the pool (its stop_line and hard_line, and its trigger_line when it writes one): no set of the instance names it.

default.description: Neither the instance nor the catalog gives the pool lines: the stop line is the capacity, the hard line 0 and the trigger line the capacity.

consumption_source.description: Where the amount of a task's consumption of a pool read from a fact comes from in an evaluation, a value of pool_line_held, capped_spend, resource_reserve_insufficient and pool_lines_unspendable, beside consumption, whenever the reason's task's consumption of its pool is read from a fact (#428 SCHED-C1f1, contracts/scheduling/README.md "A run's consumption read from a fact"). A constant consumption carries neither.

fact.description: The value of the fact's usable record in the instance's scope: present at a confidence above 0, not past its own expiry, not invalidated by a reset since, an integer in 1..=2^53-1 and at most a constant capacity of the pool.

fallback.description: The entry's fallback: the instance holds no usable record of the fact (none, expired, invalidated by a reset, or present but not usable, which consumption_fact_unusable says).

refresh_limit.description: Which limit holds an instance's recognition maintenance package back (Workflow #384 D2-S4).

daily_limit.description: The package's dispatches today reached scheduling.fact_refresh.daily_limit.

failure_pause.description: Its failed runs in a row reached scheduling.fact_refresh.max_consecutive_failures today.

schedulable_state.description: The instance's schedulable-pack state does not include the package now.

activity_window.description: The instance's activity window is closed or its activity budget spent.

placement.description: The instance cannot place the package.

entry_problem.description: Why a contained task's entry page set is refused at admission (Workflow #373 NAV-3b).

empty.description: The entry page set names no page.

too_many.description: The entry page set names more than 16 pages.

duplicate.description: The entry page set names one page twice.

any_in_set.description: The entry page set names any, which only a single entry page may be.

unresolved.description: A page of the entry page set is blank or is not exactly one page of the package's page set.

phase_start_missing.description: No stage of the phased route lists an operation from a page of the entry page set.

phase_start_ambiguous.description: More than one stage of the phased route lists an operation from a page of the entry page set.

event_type.description: A ledger event type; each has the category a record without an outcome takes.

receipt_state.description: The state of an IPC receipt.

claim_kind.description: Who holds an instance or waits for it, in the one queue per instance (Workflow #369).

startup_package.description: An instance's startup package after an emulator start.

autostart.description: A configured emulator start at daemon start.

direct_task_run.description: A direct task run from the CLI, the console or MCP.

input_lifecycle.description: A safe reset or an application lifecycle command.

resume_reconnect.description: The reconnect of an instance resume.

backend_switch.description: The switch of an instance's touch and capture backends (#402 HS-2).

daemon_start_preparation.description: The dedicated preparation lease of a connection preparation.

resource_close.description: A dedicated retained-session or pause close lease.

slot.description: A program slot (the wire spelling of InstallSlot).

text_read_budget.description: Which per-consumer text read budget of located OCR text ran out (Workflow #396 REC-1).

calls.description: The provider calls of one consumer.

area.description: The summed region area of one consumer, in pixels.

target_kind.description: Which kind of target a uniqueness check compared (Workflow #396 REC-2).

template.description: A template target: positions of its match score.

ocr.description: A locate OCR target: text blocks and their confidence.

value_side.description: Which side of a value test could not be read (Workflow #396 REC-6).

right.description: The right side, another read value.

value_problem.description: Why one side of a value test could not be read (Workflow #396 REC-6).

invalid.description: The text is not in the declared format.

overflow.description: The number does not fit 64 bits.

out_of_range.description: The value lies outside the declared min..=max.

region_unresolved.description: The OCR target's region could not be resolved on the frame.

low_confidence.description: The read's confidence is missing or below the OCR target's minimum_confidence.

no_agreement.description: The frames of a declared agreement did not read one value often enough.

value_op.description: The comparison of a value test (Workflow #396 REC-6).

parses.description: The left side reads in its format.

follow_problem.description: Why a Lab recording's click that follows a template mark (Workflow #396 REC-4) or a located-text mark (#463 L2) does not hold.

not_template.description: The followed mark is neither a template mark nor a located-text mark of the step.

not_required.description: The followed mark is only a member of an any_of check of the step's page.

guard_conflict.description: The click guard names another mark than the followed one.

primary_mismatch.description: On the primary frame the template's best match is not at its crop, or not at factor 1000.

template_unmatched.description: On a frame the template does not pass in its search area.

click_outside_frame.description: On a frame the click box that follows the match or the found text leaves the frame.

press_outside_found_box.description: On the primary frame the press of the step's executed click lies outside the box the followed located text gives there (#463 L2).

page_needs_followed_text.description: The step's page would need the followed located text to be recognized: no other mark of the step recognizes it, or a check of the page names the located text (#463 L2 fix 1).

select_problem.description: Why a Lab recording step's select, a choice in a list of fixed slots by the name read in each (#463 R1), cannot be declared or generated.

with_follow.description: The request's click follows a mark beside the select: the select's click is the slot it chooses.

with_gesture.description: The request or the step declares a drag, a long press or another gesture: a select taps once.

with_click.description: The request declares a click rectangle or a click source beside the select: the select's click is the slot it chooses.

with_retry.description: The request or the step declares a click retry: a select step declares no retry.

on_optional_step.description: The step is optional, or the request makes it optional: a select step's page is its list.

with_application.description: The request or the step declares an application operation: one step has one effect.

on_final_step.description: The stopped recording's last step: the package ends on its page, which then would be the select's empty end too.

slot_outside_frame.description: A slot's rectangle, click box or name region does not lie inside the frame.

name_id_invalid.description: A name's id breaks the grammar ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$.

wanted_name_invalid.description: The wanted value's name breaks the grammar ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$.

name_duplicate.description: Two names of the select have one id.

default_not_in_names.description: The wanted value's default is no id of the select's names.

pressed_not_in_names.description: pressed is no id of the select's names.

wanted_name_taken.description: Another select step of the recording names its wanted value alike.

on_empty_key_reserved.description: The on_empty key is <task_id>_done, the key of the run's usual end.

on_empty_key_taken.description: The on_empty key is another select step's of the recording.

guard_missing.description: The step's page has no template, color, color digest or check mark (or a value test named as its click guard): a select step needs a guard.

kernel_refused.description: The kernel's admission refuses the select step as record stop would generate it.

no_select.description: clear_select names a step that has no select, so there is nothing to take off (#463 R2).

on_empty_key_of_ending.description: The on_empty key is the outcome key of an ending of the recording (#463 R2 fix 1).

choice_not_refined.description: record stop meets a step marked as holding a choice that no select refines yet: it knows no names, so no package is generated (#463 S2-6).

no_choice.description: A request's choice false names a step that is not marked as holding a choice, so there is nothing to take off (#463 S2-6 fix round 1).

drop_of_choice.description: drop_step names a step that holds a choice (marked as holding one, or refined by a select), the last step too: its press may have chosen the item already selected, which changes nothing on the screen and still matters to a run handed another value; the choice is withdrawn first (#463 stage two, train, fix round).

transition_of_choice.description: to_transition names a step that holds a choice (marked as holding one, or refined by a select): a page transition holds none, so the conversion would lose it; the choice is withdrawn first (#463 stage two, train, fix round).

scan_without_fold.description: A scrolling select (rows and scan) on a step that holds no fold of the swipes recorded before it: it has no screens of the list to read (#463 S2-9a, since 0.12.70).

rows_with_slots.description: The request declares rows and slots, which exclude each other (#463 S2-9a, since 0.12.70).

confirm_with_rows.description: The request declares confirm beside rows: the kernel confirms a scrolled choice itself (#463 S2-9a, since 0.12.70).

scan_stop_missing.description: The request's scan states no stop, the kind of the scrolling choice (#463 S2-9a, since 0.12.70).

scan_region_outside_frame.description: A region of a scrolling select (its list, row, anchor, name, click box, start or end mark) does not lie inside the frame (#463 S2-9a, since 0.12.70).

scan_region_outside_list.description: The row of a scrolling select does not lie inside its list (#463 S2-9a, since 0.12.70).

scan_region_outside_row.description: The anchor, the name region or the click box of a scrolling select does not lie inside its row (#463 S2-9a, since 0.12.70).

scan_number_not_measured.description: A number the Lab measures from the demonstration cannot be measured there (a swipe recorded without its after loop's record) and the request does not give it in scan.numbers (#463 S2-9a, since 0.12.70).

on_empty_without_end.description: A scrolling select straight to the wanted item (scan.stop wanted) that declares no end mark gives an on_empty_key: such a scan never reads its list to an end, so a run cannot end normally there; where the item is not found it fails with the kernel's selection_scan_early_stop_unreached (#463 S2-9b, since 0.12.70).

scan_swipe_too_long.description: The first forward swipe of the fold, the package's advance, moves the finger further along the list than the kernel's admission allows (the list's length less a row's, less one), which no given number changes; details displacement_px and most_px; the scroll is recorded again with shorter swipes, so that neighbouring screens share at least one row (#463 S2-9a fix round 1, since 0.12.70).

ending_problem.description: Why an ending of a stopped Lab recording, a screen that ends the business another way after its last press (#463 R2), cannot be taken, given up or generated.

recording_active.description: The recording is active: an ending is taken after record stop, which records the usual ending first.

with_other_change.description: The request names a step change beside ending or remove_ending, or both of these.

key_invalid.description: The outcome key breaks the grammar ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_]{0,127}$.

key_reserved.description: The outcome key is <task_id>_done, the key of the run's usual end.

key_of_select.description: The outcome key is the on_empty key of a select step of the recording.

key_exists.description: Another ending of the recording has the outcome key.

key_unknown.description: remove_ending names a key no ending of the recording has.

page_exists.description: Another ending of the recording has the page name.

no_marks.description: The ending adds and reuses no mark, so its page would recognize nothing.

ocr_alone_unchecked.description: record stop's self-check item 9 could not check the ending: its page rests on OCR marks alone and the Lab had no OCR model, so whether it passes on a screen the run may show instead is unknown (fix 1).

ending_against.description: The recorded screen an ending's page passes on that it must not pass on (#463 R2, record stop's self-check item 9).

previous.description: The frames of a step after whose press the run awaits the endings (its page, or its page transition's frames when it has one): the result of that press has not shown yet.

usual.description: The frames of the last step, the usual ending: the ending would always win there.

other_ending.description: The frames of another ending of the recording.

optional_after_problem.description: Why an optional step a stopped Lab recording inserts after the effect of one of its steps, a pop-up after which the path goes on (#463 R4), cannot be inserted or given up.

recording_active.description: The recording is active: a step is inserted after record stop, which generated the package of the recorded path first.

with_other_change.description: The request names another change beside optional_after or remove_inserted, or both of these.

step_unknown.description: optional_after.step names no step of the recording (none, a dropped or a converted one).

step_last.description: optional_after.step names the last step: every run ends on its page, after which nothing is pressed.

step_application.description: optional_after.step names a step whose effect is an application operation.

no_marks.description: The inserted step adds and reuses no mark, so its page would recognize nothing.

no_effect.description: #463 KR-1 (since 0.12.70, in place of no_click): the inserted step declares no effect, neither a click nor a key, so nothing would close its pop-up.

clears_optional.description: The request clears optional on an inserted step: a step never recorded on the path stays optional.

not_inserted.description: remove_inserted names no inserted step of the recording that is not given up yet.

ready_missing.description: One pre-check of record stop that a Lab recording fails, as record ready lists it in missing[].what (#463 S2-1): one word per pre-check, one cause per word; record stop answers its code.

too_few_steps.description: The recording has fewer than two effective steps (record_no_steps).

application_entry_not_first.description: A step after the first is an application entry step, which has no frame (record_application_entry_not_first).

effect_missing.description: A step before the last has no effect: no click, select or application operation (record_step_click_missing).

final_has_effect.description: The last step has an effect; it only recognizes the screen the package arrives at (record_final_step_has_click).

page_recognition.description: A step but the application entry step has no own or reused mark (record_step_without_recognition).

transition_recognition.description: A step's page transition has no own or reused mark (record_step_without_recognition with transition page).

too_many_effects.description: More steps have an effect than a package holds (record_too_many_steps).

game.description: The package's game is known neither from record stop nor from the recording nor from the Lab's instance configuration nor (#463 S2-1b) from the configuration of the installation the program runs from (record_locale_missing).

server.description: The package's server is known neither from record stop nor from the recording nor from the Lab's instance configuration nor (#463 S2-1b) from the configuration of the installation the program runs from (record_locale_missing).

locale.description: The package's locale is known neither from record stop nor from the recording (record_locale_missing).

effect_after_stop.description: After a step that stops the application the next effect is no launch or restart (record_step_after_stop_invalid).

reused_mark_missing.description: A step's page or its page transition reuses a mark that is no mark of an effective step (record_mark_rejected, reuse_source_missing).

forbidden_mark_missing.description: A step forbids a mark that is no mark of an effective step (record_mark_rejected, forbidden_source_missing).

anchor_not_own_template.description: A step's anchor is no own template mark of it (record_mark_rejected, anchor_invalid).

application_without_home.description: The last launch or restart is followed by no step that is the main interface (record_application_without_home).

optional_restart_home.description: The main interface after the last launch or restart is optional (record_optional_restart_segment_end).

select_optional.description: A select step is optional (record_select_invalid, on_optional_step).

select_retry.description: A select step's click declares a retry (record_select_invalid, with_retry).

select_gesture.description: A select step's click declares a gesture (record_select_invalid, with_gesture).

select_follow.description: A select step's click follows a mark (record_select_invalid, with_follow).

select_key_reserved.description: A select step's on_empty key is the usual ending's (record_select_invalid, on_empty_key_reserved).

select_key_taken.description: A select step's on_empty key is another select step's (record_select_invalid, on_empty_key_taken).

select_wanted_taken.description: A select step's wanted name is another select step's (record_select_invalid, wanted_name_taken).

ending_key_reserved.description: An ending's outcome key is the usual ending's (record_ending_invalid, key_reserved).

ending_key_of_select.description: An ending's outcome key is a select step's on_empty key (record_ending_invalid, key_of_select).

ending_key_taken.description: An ending's outcome key is another ending's (record_ending_invalid, key_exists).

ending_page_taken.description: An ending's page name is another ending's (record_ending_invalid, page_exists).

ending_mark_missing.description: An ending's page reuses a mark that is no mark of an effective step (record_mark_rejected, reuse_source_missing).

size_not_base.description: Workflow #392 DA-5cd fix round 1: the recording holds frames that are not the base size (record_size_not_base).

select_unrefined.description: #463 S2-6: a step marked as holding a choice that no select refines yet (record_select_invalid, choice_not_refined).

scan_without_select.description: #463 S2-8' (since 0.12.70): a press step whose recorded swipes are folded into its scrolling search declares no scrolling select yet (record_scan_invalid, scan_not_selected).

scan_end_not_recorded.description: #463 S2-9a (since 0.12.70): a scrolling select that reads its list to its end declares no end mark: the demonstration never reached the list's end (record_scan_invalid, end_not_recorded).

key_guard_missing.description: #463 KR-1 (since 0.12.70): a step that presses a key gets no guard (record_key_invalid, guard_missing; fix round 1: by a click step's rule, its page gives none).

ready_check.description: One self-check of record stop, in the order they run, as record ready names it in checks_after and in the what of a self-check's refusal (#463 S2-1).

frames.description: Every live frame and template crop is read back with its recorded sha256 and the recording's size.

admission.description: The generated package is admitted by the kernel and gives its evaluator.

first_decision.description: The offline simulation of the package's first step on its recorded frames.

cross_check.description: Every page on its own frames, the guards on located text, the optional steps, the arrival gates and the entry overlay.

endings.description: Every ending's page on its own frames and on the screens a run may show instead.

selects.description: Every select step's decisions on its own frames.

final_package.description: The final package: encoded, expanded again, admitted again, and the same first decision.

cases.description: #463 S2-10 (since 0.12.70): the regression cases made from the recording (one per step with a press and a page, the final screen, one per ending), each run on the final package by the one runner of the case contract before it is written; the last check, run only when every other passed.

case_limit.description: A limit the regression cases record stop writes beside its package say of themselves, in lab.cases.limits (#463 S2-10, since 0.12.70); it informs and refuses nothing.

self_agreement.description: The cases were made from the frames the package was built from: that they pass shows the package recognises the screens it was recorded on and says nothing about screens it did not meet.

key_problem.description: Why a Lab recording step's key, the back key a step presses in place of a click, declared after the fact and never sent while recording, cannot be declared or generated (record_key_invalid; #463 KR-1, since 0.12.70).

word_unknown.description: The key's word is none of the vocabulary's, which is back alone.

with_click.description: The request declares a click beside the key (a rectangle, a source mark, a followed mark, a gesture or a press box), or an inserted step declares both a click and a key.

with_application.description: The request declares an application operation beside the key.

with_retry.description: The request declares a click retry beside the key: a key step declares no retry.

application_entry.description: The step is the application entry step, which has no frame and no page to guard a key on.

application_step.description: The step's effect is an application operation, declared or executed.

holds_choice.description: A key and a choice on one step: the step holds a choice (a select or a choice mark), or the request gives one to a step with a key or beside a key.

step_not_effective.description: The step is dropped or converted into a page transition.

guard_missing.description: record stop meets a step that presses a key and gets no guard (fix round 1: by a click step's rule, it names none its page requires and its page requires no template, colour, colour digest or check mark): a key has no coordinate to trust.

holds_fold.description: The train of 0.12.70 (#463 S2-8' joined): the step holds a fold, the swipes recorded before it folded into its scrolling search, so its press is the press of a scrolling search; the fold is undone first.
