orientation_mismatch.description: The frame disagrees with the package's orientation, and its display does too or no rotation says it is a turned frame of an agreeing display: the application is not in its orientation yet. Until Workflow #392 DA-2b the run ends with it (as it ended with the retired contained_task_frame_resolution_mismatch); DA-2b makes it only the cause under the run's own end.

translation_unsupported.description: The map moves regions (a translation, or a frame cropped from its display), which this Runtime does not map yet: translations and crops come with Workflow #392 DA-2b. The kernel's frame gate refuses the frame and the run ends with no input.

input_scale_unsupported.description: The frame's map is not the plain identity (a pure scale) and the input side does not map the input to the device frame: the host sends nothing and the run ends. Until Workflow #392 DA-3 every input under a pure scale; from DA-3 every input under a pure scale whose double is not a whole number (a point on a box's edge could map outside the box's device box); from DA-3 until Workflow #392 DA-5ab also every input of a Lab declared operation on a frame of another size than its package, which DA-5ab sends under the frame's map as a run's input, so that a Lab operation's input too is refused only under such a scale. From DA-3 until Workflow #392 DA-3b also a vertical-brake drag under any scale, whose brake the contract holds at exactly 100 pixels while the map would change it; DA-3b sends that drag as a drag with a pause and a brake.

safe_area_unavailable.description: The game's display declaration measures on the safe area and the frame's geometry has no insets: a handset that declares no device model (Workflow #392 DA-4b-D: no capture backend reads a cutout; an emulator's insets are 0): the value of contained_task_geometry_unavailable, and of display_map_unresolved where a frame reaches the kernel's gate without the host's check.

safe_area_declaration_invalid.description: Workflow #392 DA-4b-D: the safe-area declaration directory (display_safe_area.directory) or one of its files cannot be read, or a file breaks actingcommand.display-safe-area.v1; path names it, json_pointer the first member that breaks the schema (empty for the whole document).

safe_area_model_repeated.description: Workflow #392 DA-4b-D: two safe-area declaration files declare one device model; path and other_path name them.

safe_area_model_undeclared.description: Workflow #392 DA-4b-D: no safe-area declaration file declares the device model the instance declares; config_key names the setting the model was read from, path the directory.

safe_area_form_undeclared.description: Workflow #392 DA-4b-D: the declaration file of the instance's device model (path) covers no display size and rotation the frame shows.

player_hold_phase.description: Where a player hold stands (Workflow #429 R-7a, contracts/player-hold.md).

requesting.description: The gate is closed; queued operator and client entries end.

draining.description: The instance's in-flight runs drain to a checkpoint.

handing_back.description: The device is handed back and its session closed.

held.description: The Runtime touches the device not at all.

releasing.description: The release takes its reconnect claim and lifts the hold.

player_hold_next.description: What a release of a player hold did next (Workflow #429 R-7a, contracts/player-hold.md).

reconnected.description: No pause held the instance: it was reconnected and self-checked.

instance_paused.description: The instance's own pause holds it: nothing was touched. First when both pauses are in effect (R-7a section 2.6).

scheduling_paused.description: Only the global pause holds it: nothing was touched.

instance_gate.description: One control gate of an instance, in the one order of R-7a section 2.6 (registered in that order) (Workflow #429 R-7a, contracts/player-hold.md).

player_hold.description: 1: the instance's player hold, any phase.

instance_pause.description: 2: the instance's own scheduling pause, any stage.

resource_fence.description: 4: the instance's #403 resource fence, any state.

control_gate_code.description: The effective code of a control gate: each token is the spelling of the runtime-host code the gate defers a dispatch with; the contract derives it, the host emits the code (Workflow #429 R-7a, contracts/player-hold.md).

player_hold_operation_kind.description: The kind of a player hold operation (Workflow #429 R-7a, contracts/player-hold.md).

player_hold_operation_state.description: The state of a player hold operation record (Workflow #429 R-7a, contracts/player-hold.md).

failed.description: Ended in a failure after it was accepted.

player_hold_restored_from.description: Whether a restored player hold had finished its hand-back before the stop (Workflow #429 R-7a, contracts/player-hold.md).

acquiring.description: The Runtime stopped during the acquire: the device was not confirmed reset.

player_hold_startup_package.description: What a release of a player hold did with the startup package (Workflow #429 R-7a, contracts/player-hold.md).

scheduled.description: A new startup package claim was queued (behind the pause when one holds it).

cancelled.description: skip cancelled a queued startup package claim and ended its W2-B row.

player_hold_source_actor.description: Who asked for a player hold operation: the envelope, one of the source gate's three (Workflow #429 R-7a, contracts/player-hold.md).

cli.description: (Cli, Cli): actingctl, and MCP on the channel mcp.

player_hold_settlement_trigger.description: Why a client settles a player hold request from Status (Workflow #429 R-7a, contracts/player-hold.md).

dropped.description: The connection ended before the receipt header of the frame the call wrote.

reopened.description: Any other failure after sending, or the sending process is gone; the trigger a stored attempt carries.

player_hold_settlement_verdict.description: A player hold settlement's verdict (Workflow #429 R-7a, contracts/player-hold.md).

settled.description: Status confirmed the request's final state or that it was not performed.

unsupported.description: An older Runtime dropped the frame (rows A7, R8).

player_hold_settlement_outcome.description: What a settled player hold request did (Workflow #429 R-7a, contracts/player-hold.md).

failed.description: It failed after it was accepted.

not_performed.description: It was not performed and will not be.

hold_ended.description: The hold is gone; who ended it is not known.

player_hold_unconfirmed_observed.description: What an unconfirmed player hold settlement saw; the first three are not final (Workflow #429 R-7a, contracts/player-hold.md).

in_progress.description: Its own record is running. Not final.

in_progress_other.description: Another counter's release is under way. Not final.

status_unreadable.description: Status could not be read. Not final.

epoch_changed.description: The Runtime restarted and nothing shows the request. Final.

instance_not_listed.description: Status does not list the instance. Final.

inconsistent.description: The hold is the request's own but in its acquire without its record. Final.

not_registered.description: No record: refused at entry or not yet read. Final, though a later Status may still show it.

player_hold_settlement_rule.description: The row of the player hold settlement table that decided, for tests and diagnosis (Workflow #429 R-7a, contracts/player-hold.md).

run_origin.description: Who started a run that a client cannot stop, the value of a StopInstanceRun's refusal scheduled_contained_task_not_client_cancellable (Workflow #429 R-6, contracts/runtime-interface.md "Workbench request kinds"). Since 0.12.55 (Workflow #429 R-6b2) the refusal names host only: a policy run is stopped and settles as a stop.

policy.description: A run the scheduler dispatched. The first slice of R-6 (0.12.53) refused it with this token; since 0.12.55 (Workflow #429 R-6b2, ledger revision 8) StopInstanceRun stops it and no longer produces the token, which stays registered.

host.description: A run the Runtime starts for itself: a startup package, a recovery ladder rung or an idle action's rest; a pause or a person's hold stops it.

state_problem.description: Which kind of invalid state ended a contained task's run with contained_task_state_invalid, the code's value state_problem (Workflow #428 DIAG-SI, register 1.320, since 0.12.55). The kernel and the host emit the code at many places; each gives its kind and, where it knows them, the page (page_id), the operation (pack_operation_id) and the stage (phase_id).

no_move_from_page.description: No operation of the stage the run is in (of the package, for a route without stages) leaves the page the run observes, and the page is no target and no error page of the package: an authoring error of the package. page_id names the page and phase_id the stage.

transition_refused.description: The run's state machine refused a transition the kernel asked of it in its state (run_transition_invalid inside the kernel): a Runtime-internal fault.

runtime_invariant.description: A Runtime-internal invariant broke: a value that cannot be absent was absent, an arithmetic that cannot fail failed, or an answer that is never given was given (a pacing factor below 1000, a confirmation that held a step that is no wait step, a Lab operation's own bookkeeping).

held_state_unusable.description: A state the run's layers or a package registry hold is not one the host can use: the run's navigation or interrupt state, a layer package the run admitted, or a registry's return-home entry without a listed package.

held_state.description: How a held pair stood when task_held reported it, the not-run explanation row's eligibility (Workflow #438 HELD-1, contracts/scheduling/README.md "Held records"). A held code never comes with eligibility false.

due.description: Eligibility true: the pair is due (its trigger true and its stop false) and the held code holds it.

undecidable.description: Eligibility unknown: whether the pair is due cannot be decided (an unknown trigger or stop, or a fact refresh wait after one).

held_end.description: How a hold that task_held reported ended, the value of task_held_ended (Workflow #438 HELD-1, contracts/scheduling/README.md "Held records", "The end").

selected.description: The evaluation selected the pair's decision; whether its intent is then admitted is the dispatch records'.

why_changed.description: The pair's row carries another why code, held or not (a trigger turned false, a package closed, a pause), or a fact refresh wait of another fact_key; a move between the three waits for one fact's refresh of the same fact_key is none.

row_gone.description: The instance has rows and none of the pair: the task left the catalog generation, or its package left the composed catalog.

instance_gone.description: The evaluation decided nothing for the instance: it left the snapshot.

restarted.description: The hold was reported by an earlier run of the Runtime: the start ended it before recording its settlement anchor; held_for_ms is absent.

device_group_problem.description: Which rule of device groups the instances[] entries that share one device break, the value device_group_problem of device_group_config_invalid (Workflow #437 MAPP-1, register 1.323 and 1.328, contracts/device-group.md "The configuration form", since 0.12.56).

name_invalid.description: An entry's device_group is not a name of 1 to 64 bytes under the alias rules (empty, longer than 64 bytes, or holding a control character). The first of the group checks, on every entry that names a group, before the kind rules; aliases is the entry and config_key is device_group.

device_mismatch.description: The members of a group of several name the device by different keys or values: all must name the same instance_index, all the same instance_name, or all the same host and port (and serial when one is named). config_key is the key that differs.

handset_member.description: A member of a group of several is a handset (device.kind handset): the private binding file binds one serial to one alias. config_key is device.

fixture_member.description: A member of a group of several is a fixture entry. config_key is fixture_backend.

application_shared.description: Two members of a group of several have one application_id; the members are told apart by package name. config_key is application_id.

startup_package_missing.description: A member of a group of several declares no startup_package, the one way the Runtime reaches a member's home. config_key is startup_package.

device_action_unsupported.description: A member of a group of several turns on a device-level action the first slice does not make group-aware: start_emulator true, an idle.action in effect other than none, or a ladder profile in effect whose rungs hold emulator_restart. config_key is start_emulator, idle.action or recovery_ladder_profile.

undeclared_shared_device.description: Two entries outside one device group name the same device: the same instance_index, instance_name, serial, or host and port at assembly, or the same discovered index or ADB port after the start's discovery. config_key is the shared key.

several_members_unsupported.description: A group of several that breaks no other rule, refused at load by every build before the slice "order within one device". config_key is device_group.

device_group_wait.description: Why a member of a device group waits for its device, the value device_group_wait of device_group_waiting (Workflow #437 MAPP-1, contracts/device-group.md "One pick per device per round", since 0.12.56).

selected.description: The other member's candidate (task_id) won the device this round.

held.description: A claim or a run of the other member holds the device, or waits for it first (holder_kind the claim kind; task_id with a run).

player_hold.description: A person holds the device through the other member.

fenced.description: The other member is fenced; its fence holds the whole group until it is lifted.

close_unconfirmed.description: Since 0.12.67 (Workflow #437 G1): the other member is fenced for resources of its own whose state could not be confirmed (a close, an ADB check's clean-up or a contained failure left them so), and the device is held for it: no other member is given the device until its fence is lifted. It comes before fenced.

application_switch_step.description: Which step of the switch before a run failed, the value application_switch_step of application_switch_failed (Workflow #437 MAPP-2a, contracts/device-group.md "The switch before a run", since 0.12.59; lease_renewal since 0.12.60, MAPP-2d).

foreground_read.description: The read of the package in front through the member's registration failed: its ADB query did not answer (failure_code application_foreground_unknown), or an unconfirmed ADB cleanup fenced the member (instance_resources_fenced).

stop.description: The stop of another member's application under the run's key failed or was refused (application_id is that member's package): its own failure records are written, and a key that is not the device's, or a member outside the holder's group, is refused before any device step.

startup_package.description: The member's startup package on the run's key did not reach its home, or was refused before it ran: no startup package, its admission, its ADB readiness, a key with too little time left for the startup run (for a run's switch since 0.12.60, no more than the heartbeat reserve; for a caller that states the time it still needs, less than the startup run's lease time and that time), or the key lost during the startup run.

lease_renewal.description: The run's renewal of its lease after the startup run handed the key back was refused or failed: the lease lost, lapsed or taken over (failure_code the scheduler's refusal). The member's application was started and no task of the run ran (Workflow #437 MAPP-2d, since 0.12.60).

variable_source.description: Where the value a policy run reads of a package's variable comes from, the value variable_source of a variable_values record (Workflow #463 V2, contracts/package-variables.md "The run", since 0.12.61).

set.description: The application's entry row of the variable's name in its session.resource_targets v3 record, the value a person or an agent set.

variable_problem.description: Why the value set on an application for a package's variable was not handed to a run, which reads the default instead: the value variable_problem of goal_value_not_applied and of a variable_values record; and keys_left_out, an ordered value handed to the run in part, on its record only (Workflow #463 V2, contracts/package-variables.md "The run", since 0.12.61).

not_an_option.description: A choice value that is none of the declaration's options.

out_of_range.description: An integer value below the declaration's min or above its max.

off_step.description: An integer value within the range but on no step from min.

type_changed.description: A value that is not of the variable's type: no string for a choice, no whole number for an integer, no boolean for a switch, no list of strings for an ordered variable.

keys_removed.description: An ordered value whose keys the declaration still offers are fewer than min_count once the others are left out.

count_out_of_range.description: An ordered value of offered keys only whose count is below min_count, or whose offered keys are more than max_count.

key_repeated.description: An ordered value that names one key twice.

keys_left_out.description: An ordered value naming keys the declaration no longer offers, whose offered keys are enough: the run reads those in their order, the source stays set, and no warning is written, since the value was applied in part.

entry_unreadable.description: The application's entry row of the name holds a value, but who set it (its set_unix_ms or its channel) could not be read: the value is not applied.

irreversible_by_root.description: A package of the game root that declares the variable counts as able to do something irreversible by the whole root (the root check's variable_irreversible_by_root): it provides, or its remedies list, a capability a package of the root marks irreversible.

package_unreadable.description: A package of the game root could not be read, so the root check counts every package of the root as able to do something irreversible (its variable_irreversible_by_root, the safe side), while no package that declares the variable provides or lists a capability marked irreversible.

goals_unreadable.description: The game root's goals.json could not be read (an I/O failure other than its absence), so which names it takes is not known.

declaration_conflict.description: Packages of the game root declare the name differently (the root check's variable_conflict at a declaration).

goal_name_conflict.description: An entry of the game root's goals.json uses the name for anything but its placement (the root check's variable_conflict at the name).

name_out_of_limits.description: The name is the game root's 97th or later (the root check's variable_out_of_limits).

cap_range.description: A package reads the variable as a designated effect's cap and it is no integer from 0 to 1000 (the root check's variable_cap_range).

root_unchecked.description: No root check judges the variable for the application's game now, so nothing says whether the variable applies. With a composed standard pack (fix round 2) the scheduler workbench has noted the game uncomposed: at a check its root failed its check, or the composition was refused (for this root, for another game's root, or as a whole, as for its size) while the generation in force did not hold the game with its present files, so a sound root that was judged reads root_unchecked too while another game's root keeps the composition from succeeding. A later check does not lift the note by itself: it is lifted only by a check whose composition of every game succeeds and is activated. Without one, the Runtime's table of the bound packages was built before an instance of that game was known.

goals_failure.description: Why a game root's goals.json is not applied while the root runs, the value goals_failure of standard_pack_goals_not_applied (Workflow #463 V2 fix round 2, contracts/package-variables.md "A variable that does not apply", since 0.12.61).

refused.description: The contract crate's reader refused the file: it applies no entry and takes no name.

unreadable.description: The file could not be read (an I/O failure other than its absence): which names it takes is not known, so no variable of the root applies.

adopt_problem.description: Which check of actinglab standard-pack adopt refused, the value adopt_problem of adopt_refused (Workflow #464 P1, contracts/standard-pack-authoring.md "The checks", since 0.12.61).

repository_invalid.description: --repo holds no applications.json, maintenance.json or packs directory, one of them or its schedule.json does not read, or a .part of a root file an interrupted adoption left is there (the message names every leftover and what to do), or, without a decision and with --replace, schedule.json gives the package a held entry beside its maintenance.json entry (two roles, which only an adoption interrupted between its two renames leaves; a rule beside that entry is the package's one maintenance role, never a second one).

recording_not_current.description: The recording --record-id names is not as its last record stop left it: no recording.json, not stopped, marked again since, or without its package. Workflow #463 S3-17 (since 0.12.71): judged by record ready's one function, a status other than packaged (the details' record_ready, that function's answer with its missing); where that function cannot read the recording, its status and amended_at_unix_ms checked as before (its refusal the cause); its artifact and its package's file checked as before; and a cases directory beside the package that cannot be listed (Workflow #463 AC-1).

package_invalid.description: The package is not admitted as package preflight admits it, or its package_id names no directory packs/<package_id>.

package_mismatch.description: The package's game is not applications.json's, or its server is none of that file's servers.

pack_exists.description: The package was adopted before (its directory, its rule, its held entry or its maintenance entry is there; the message names which, and with its directory alone either the root file adopt does not write that gives it a role and what the call accepts for it, or that an adoption was interrupted before it wrote the root files) and --replace is not given, its .part an interrupted adoption left is there (the message names every leftover and what to do), or the kept copy's place is taken. Workflow #463 AC-1 (since 0.12.71), when the adoption takes cases: a case of the package an earlier adoption took from a recording is in regression/<game>/ and --replace is not given; the .part of a case of the package an interrupted adoption left is there; or the kept place of the earlier cases is taken.

pack_dirty.description: With --replace, the version control shows a change not committed below packs/<package_id>, or cannot tell.

recording_unreviewed.description: The package is not run through (its provenance is no recording's, its cross-check did not pass, its first decision was not evaluated, or a step needs review) and the class is not held.

local_path.description: A text file of the package holds an absolute local path or the state directory.

decision_invalid.description: The decision document breaks its schema, misses a member the class or a first adoption needs (a business rule's value, which only a follower of a chain may leave out), names a pool the file does not declare, names a derived member that cannot be derived without it, says pending for a follower of a chain, gives the class business beside a maintenance role a root file adopt does not write gives the package; or a key the schedule as compiled reads of the rule's own outcome (a rule's trigger or feedback_stop, a pool's observation, an activity target's measure), or a key the rule reads of another task's outcome, is one the package of the task read does not declare.

value_origin_model.description: The decision's value names the origin model, which only the model's export writes; the number is given with the origin pack, or the value is pending.

rule_refused.description: The composer refuses schedule.json as it would be written, or the adopted package comes out unclassified.

root_file_not_canonical.description: schedule.json or maintenance.json must change and is not in the canonical form package fmt writes.

replace_across_volumes.description: With --replace, the replaced pack directory's kept place under the state directory lies on another volume than the checkout, where it cannot be moved, or the volume cannot be told; a --state-dir on the checkout's volume is given instead (and a recording's own directory by --session-state-dir, which adopt only reads, Workflow #463 AD-1 since 0.12.72, or its package by --package). Workflow #463 AC-1 (since 0.12.71): so does the kept place of the earlier cases of the package (entry the first of them).

check_tree_unmarked.description: The place of the checkout's check tree under the state directory holds no marker the tool wrote, so it is not the tool's own scratch and nothing in it is touched.

check_tree_busy.description: Another adoption of the same checkout with the same state directory holds the checkout's check tree.

check_tree_link.description: The place of the checkout's check tree under the state directory, or a directory beside it named as one a call makes the tree whole in, is a link (a symbolic link or a junction), so nothing is cleared through it or where it points.

business_rule_in_the_way.description: A decision of the class maintenance by its uses alone, without a trigger, meets the package's business rule in schedule.json (a rule the composer judges by its value), which adopt does not turn into a maintenance rule unasked; the refusal names the rule.

case_name_invalid.description: Workflow #463 AC-1 (since 0.12.71): the name of a case of the recording's set (out/<package_id>.cases/<case>/) gives no directory <package_id>.<case> of regression/<game>/: the name holds a dot, the whole is not one path segment, or with its .part it is longer than a file name takes (255 bytes). path names the case in the recording.

case_place_taken.description: Workflow #463 AC-1 (since 0.12.71): the directory regression/<game>/<package_id>.<case> a case of the recording would be written to is there (names compared in ASCII lower case) and is no case an adoption took from a recording of this package (a case.json naming the package with a recording's source); adopt neither moves nor overwrites it. entry names it.

case_failed.description: Workflow #463 AC-1 (since 0.12.71): a regression case of the recording, run by the one runner on the package as this adoption writes it, has the verdict failed; count their number, path the recording's cases directory. Fix round 1: the details list the cases that did not pass as resource regression lists them, by its one rule: failed_total how many did not pass, cases the rows of the first of them, the failed ones first, at most resource regression's bound, without a check's detail, listed how many rows are given.

recording_not_judged.description: Workflow #463 AC-1 fix round 1 (since 0.12.71): record ready's one function refused the recording otherwise than as one the Lab cannot read whole (the state not read, the recording's identity not its own, its answer not serialized), so the recording is not judged and adoption takes none it did not judge; the Lab's refusal is the cause, path the recording's recording.json.

adopt_cases.description: Which regression cases actinglab standard-pack adopt took, the member cases.state of its answer (Workflow #463 AC-1, contracts/standard-pack-authoring.md "The cases", since 0.12.71).

taken.description: With --record-id: the cases the recording's last stop wrote beside its package, read from its out/<package_id>.cases/, each run before the first write and written into regression/<game>/<package_id>.<case>/ (none when that directory holds none).

none_found.description: With --record-id: the recording's last stop wrote no cases directory beside its package (a stop of a build before #463 S2-10), so none is taken; the adoption is as before, and next names the regression case.

package_path.description: With --package: a package given by its path carries no case, so none is read; the adoption is as before, and next names the regression case.

readiness_item.description: The thirteen readiness items of a pack, the value readiness_item of package_dispatch_waiting and package_readiness_unjudged (Workflow #464 P3, contracts/standard-pack-schedule.md "Readiness", since 0.12.61).

admitted.description: S1: the Runtime's loader admits the pack.

classified.description: S2: a rule names the pack and it is not held, or a root file gives it a maintenance role.

valued.description: S3: every rule of the pack is in the maintenance tier or declares its value (complete, or a chain follower).

composed.description: S4: the composer accepts the game's schedule.json with one instance per server.

entry_reachable.description: S5: the pack's entry is reached: an application entry, no page entry to check, a registered prerequisite package, navigation data that lists it, or its server's return-home package (for the home entry of a page-graph pack, one the kernel accepts as the Runtime's entry asks it to, fix round 2); and its prerequisite chain (its declared prerequisite packages, or the return-home fallback) passes the kernel's own predicate, as the Runtime admits it before a run.

models_named.description: S6: the models the pack's recognition targets need are named (the loader refuses a target that names none).

root_checked.description: S7 (fix round 1): standard-pack check accepts the game root, beyond what S1 and S4 tell; a refusal of their kind (package_invalid of a pack, standard_pack_root_invalid of schedule.json) is answered under them.

instance_bound.description: I1: an instance of the installation is bound to the pack's game and server.

package_revision.description: I2: the bundle's declared package range passes the rule of place at the edge, called, not copied: the installation's package range holds the declared maximum, and that maximum is the revision of what the game root carries at least (the notices directory 10, goals.json 14, a pack whose control declaration declares variables 14).

unrecorded_screen_code.description: I3: whether the live Runtime has the code for an unrecorded screen; an information line, never a refusal.

requires_known.description: I4: the live build's configuration manifest names every requires word of the game's rules.

pair_unsuspended.description: I5: no pair of the pack is suspended.

models_installed.description: I6: the installation's vision root holds the models of S6 with the identity they are named by.

readiness_problem.description: Why a readiness item keeps a pack waiting, the value readiness_problem of package_dispatch_waiting (Workflow #464 P3, contracts/standard-pack-schedule.md "Readiness", since 0.12.61).

admission_refused.description: S1: the loader refused the pack; package_invalid with the loader's refusal is the cause.

schedule_missing.description: S2: the game root holds no schedule.json, and no root file gives the pack a maintenance role.

unclassified.description: S2: no rule names the pack and no root file gives it a role; standard_pack_package_unclassified is the cause.

held.description: S2: schedule.json lists the pack in held.

value_pending.description: S3: a rule of the pack (task_id) lacks a value that is still the pending marker.

value_undeclared.description: S3: a rule of the pack (task_id) declares no value, or touches a pool (pool_id) without a valuation; standard_pack_benefit_undeclared is the cause.

head_waiting.description: S3 (fix round 1): every rule of the pack rides with another rule's chain and the pack of each head waits; task_id the follower, blocking_package_id the head's pack. A follower is not ahead of its head.

composition_refused.description: S4: the composer refuses the game's schedule.json, or standard-pack check refuses that file; standard_pack_root_invalid at the file's pointer is the cause.

prerequisite_unregistered.description: S5: the prerequisite package the pack declares is no package of the game root; the kernel's contained_task_prerequisite_unbound is the cause.

prerequisite_refused.description: S5 (fix round 1): the kernel's prerequisite chain refuses the pack's chain as the Runtime would at its first run (a layer of another game, server or resolution or one that cannot be a layer, a cycle, more than three declared layers, the step limit), or a layer's admission fails; the kernel's code or the layer's package_invalid is the cause, blocking_package_id the layer.

return_home_refused.description: S5 (fix round 2): the pack is a page-graph pack whose home entry takes its server's return-home package through no chain, and that package is one the Runtime's entry refuses at the pack's first run: the kernel's require_configured_package_id and prerequisite_incompatibility_with for a configured return-home package refuse it (another game, server or resolution, one that cannot be a layer, one that declares a prerequisite package of its own), or the loader refuses it; the kernel's code (contained_task_prerequisite_incompatible, contained_task_prerequisite_mismatch) or the package's package_invalid is the cause, blocking_package_id the return-home package.

entry_unreachable.description: S5: nothing reaches the pack's entry pages (page_ids): no prerequisite package, no navigation data that lists them, no return-home package of its server.

check_refused.description: S7 (fix round 1): standard-pack check refuses the game root at this pack, or at no pack (then every pack carries it), for a reason S1 to S6 do not judge (a navigation role, a loading copy, the notices); its refusal is the cause.

root_refused.description: S7 (fix round 1): standard-pack check refuses the game root at another pack (blocking_package_id; its refusal is the cause) and judges nothing after it, so no pack of the root is complete until the check accepts it.

instance_unbound.description: I1: no instance of the installation is bound to the pack's game.

server_unbound.description: I1: the instances bound to the pack's game are bound to other servers than the pack's.

revision_outside.description: I2: the bundle's declared package maximum (required_revision) is outside the installation's range (range_min, range_max).

revision_undeclared.description: I2 (the second merge of main): the game root carries what a later package revision brought (the notices directory, goals.json, a pack whose control declaration declares variables) and the bundle declares a lower package maximum, so place refuses the bundle at the edge; required_revision the revision it carries asks, place's refusal the cause: standard_pack_root_invalid with notice_undeclared, goal_undeclared or variable_undeclared at the root's interfaces.json, naming the first declaring pack for variables. Every pack of the root answers it.

requires_unknown.description: I4: a requires word of the game's rules is one the live build does not name; standard_pack_root_invalid schedule_requires_missing at /requires/<index> is the cause.

pair_suspended.description: I5: a pair of the pack (task_id, instance_id where told) is suspended.

model_missing.description: I6: a model the pack needs (model_name) is not installed with the identity it is named by.

readiness_unjudged.description: Why a readiness item was not judged, the value readiness_unjudged of package_readiness_unjudged; for item I3 the information line (Workflow #464 P3, contracts/standard-pack-schedule.md "Readiness", since 0.12.61).

installation_not_read.description: No installation was read: only the seven items of the game root are judged. The installation's items are judged where an installation is read (the placement plan, a follow-up) and, once the pack is live, by the scheduler's own reasons.

part_not_read.description: The installation was read, but not the part this item needs.

not_admitted.description: The loader did not admit the pack, so what its content tells is unknown.

composition_refused.description: The composer refused the game's schedule.json, so no rule is classified, valued or checked against the live build.

no_rule.description: No rule of schedule.json composes for the pack (none names it, it is held, or the root holds no schedule.json), so it has no value to judge.

server_not_told.description: The installation's reading binds instances to the pack's game without telling their servers.

package_undeclared.description: The bundle's declared package range was not given: an installed game root keeps no interfaces.json.

no_revision_tells.description: Item I3: no interface revision tells whether the live Runtime has the code for an unrecorded screen (the coordinator's ruling 3 on board #464); an information line, never a refusal.

check_stopped.description: S7 (fix round 1): standard-pack check stopped at this pack's refusal, which is answered under S1 or S4, and judged nothing after it.

readiness_state.description: A pack's answer in the readiness (its member readiness; Workflow #464 P3 fix round 1, contracts/standard-pack-schedule.md "Readiness", since 0.12.61).

waiting.description: An item fails; every failing item is listed with its problem. An item of the game root that was not judged comes only with one that fails and never counts as holding.

ready_to_place.description: Every item of the game root holds and no item of an installation fails, but not every installation item was judged (no installation was read, or not all of it): complete as far as the game root tells; the installation's items are judged where it is placed.

dispatchable.description: Every item of the game root and every item of the installation holds (I3 is information). Not included: a positive net benefit, which the scheduler judges only at run time.

not_scheduled.description: The pack plays a supporting part a root file gives it (its roles) and no rule dispatches it: other packs' runs use it.

readiness_role.description: The supporting part a root file gives a pack, the parts of standard_pack_maintenance_packages (its member roles in the readiness; Workflow #464 P3 fix round 1, since 0.12.61).

startup.description: A bundle.json maintenance[] entry's use startup.

return_home.description: A bundle.json maintenance[] entry's use return_home.

recognition.description: A bundle.json maintenance[] entry's use recognition.

chain.description: A step of navigation.json's recovery chain.

then_run.description: A package an interrupts.json then.run names.

report_part.description: Which part of a problem report could not be read, the value report_part of report_part_missing (Workflow #467 RPT-1, contracts/problem-report.md section 9, since 0.12.61).

run_listing.description: The listing of an instance's failed and unfinished runs in the window (alias the instance).

run_before.description: The listing of the run first recorded just before the newest failed or unfinished run on its instance (alias the instance).

run_status.description: A run's status, as run show reads it (request_id the run; file its run.json).

run_steps.description: A run's steps, as run evidence reads them (request_id the run; file its steps.json).

run_geometry.description: A run's task.geometry_observed records (request_id the run; file its geometry.json).

run_scores.description: The failing step's task.recognition_completed records (request_id the run; file its scores.json).

run_excerpt.description: The failing step's records of the run's diagnostic stream (request_id the run; file its overlay-excerpt.jsonl); without them the scores come from the recognition record.

frame.description: One frame of a run (request_id the run; file the frame's entry).

errors_view.description: The errors view of an instance in the window (alias the instance; file its errors.jsonl).

versions.description: The installation's bundle sources in versions.json (file versions.json).

report_part_reason.description: Why a part of a problem report is missing, the value report_part_reason of report_part_missing (Workflow #467 RPT-1, contracts/problem-report.md section 9, since 0.12.61).

not_read_to_end.description: The read stopped before its end, at its own limit or at the Runtime's read budget (for an errors view, a read the Runtime cut short): what it holds may miss what came after, and a listing that was not read to its end never says none.

budget_spent.description: The report's read budget was spent before the read began or while it ran (caused by call_budget_exhausted, or by the client's time limit once the budget was spent).

runtime_refused.description: The Runtime answered the read with its refusal (the caused_by link is the Runtime's outcome).

read_failed.description: The read failed: the connection, the client's own check, or the file system (the caused_by link is its failure).

not_recorded.description: The run records no such part: a run without a diagnostic stream.

too_large.description: The part is larger than the bound it is read with (caused by material_too_large).

unreadable.description: What was read is not what it must be: lines of the diagnostic stream that are no record, a bundle file that is no JSON (caused by foreign_data_error).

search_windows_spent.description: The errors view's search for the newest rows read its largest window of ledger sequences without reaching the window's first record: older rows of the window were not searched (summary.json's searched_from is the lowest sequence searched).

report_write_step.description: The step of writing a problem report that failed, the value report_write_step of report_write_failed (Workflow #467 RPT-1, contracts/problem-report.md section 9, since 0.12.61).

pack.description: Packing the archive in memory failed; nothing was written.

create_directory.description: The output directory could not be made (path the directory).

name_exists.description: A file of the archive's name is already there (path the archive); it is never replaced.

write_partial.description: The partial file could not be created or written (path the partial file); one that was created and is left behind is retained.

rename.description: The partial file could not be moved into place (path the archive, from_path the partial file, which is retained).

report_fit.description: Whether a problem report fits its size bound after the parts the bound may leave out were left out, the value report_fit of report_trimmed (Workflow #467 RPT-1, contracts/problem-report.md section 8, since 0.12.61).

fits.description: The archive, as written, is within its bound.

still_over.description: Every part the bound may leave out was left out and the archive, as written, is still over its bound: the parts that are never left out are larger than it.

report_output_root.description: The root a refused output directory of a problem report lies in, the value report_output_root of report_output_refused (Workflow #467 RPT-1, contracts/problem-report.md section 1, since 0.12.61).

goal_problem.description: Why an EditGoal was refused under the fact write gate, after the version comparison, the value goal_problem of goal_value_invalid, one word per situation a reader can tell apart (Workflow #463 V3, contracts/runtime-interface.md "Goal request kinds", since 0.12.61).

name_unknown.description: The name is no entry of the application's page (no entry of goals.json, no variable of a package the active catalog binds on the application, no remedy parameter of such a package) and no variable of its game root, and, for a set, the value is no other resource target {resource, at_least}; for a clear, no stored value and no target has the name; or the name has no entry name's form.

holds_no_value.description: The name is a heading or a note entry of goals.json, which holds no value.

tier_not_built.description: The name is a tier entry of goals.json: no reader of this build reads a tier's value (Workflow #455 G-R5 builds it), so none is stored.

remedy_parameter.description: The name is a remedy parameter of a bound package, which remedy set writes with the permission it scopes; the goal page shows it read-only.

variable_not_applying.description: The name is a variable that does not apply in the application's game root; variable_problem says why. No value is stored for it.

not_offered.description: Fix round 1: the name is declared in the application's game root (a placement of goals.json, or a variable a package of the root declares), but by no package the active catalog binds on the application: it is not offered there, and the page lists a placement of it not_offered. No value is stored for it.

wrong_type.description: The value is not of the entry's type, or an object of other members than its own (json_pointer names the member).

out_of_range.description: An integer value below min or above max, or a resource at_least below 1 or above the pool's capacity or the safe integers (range_min, range_max).

off_step.description: An integer value within its range but on no step from min.

not_an_option.description: A choice value, or an item of an ordered value, that is none of the declaration's options (json_pointer names the item).

key_repeated.description: An ordered value that names one key twice (json_pointer names the later one).

count_out_of_range.description: An ordered value of fewer than min_count or more than max_count keys (range_min, range_max).

value_too_large.description: The value's canonical text is longer than the store keeps, 1024 bytes (range_max).

pool_not_targetable.description: The pool of a resource value is no pool the application can target (pool_id).

pool_unvalued.description: The pool of a resource value is targetable only with its own step or importance, which a goal by name does not carry: its valuation lacks scale or gap (pool_id).

deadline_unsupported.description: A resource value carries by_unix_ms: no reader of this build reads a deadline (Workflow #455 G-R4 builds it), so none is stored.

value_not_set.description: A clear of a name that holds no stored value: nothing to clear.

record_unreadable.description: The application's stored record is neither a v2 nor a v3 record the readers read (a v1 policy, or rows the reader refuses): write its whole document with targets set first.

record_out_of_limits.description: The edited record would hold more targets (16) or entries (96) than a record keeps (range_max).

not_checked_yet.description: Fix round 1: what the page is judged by is not in the Runtime's memory yet: the scheduler workbench has not checked the game root since the start (or since the game came into use), or no evaluation has read the bound packages for the active catalog and procedure manifest. Nothing is known of the name and nothing is stored; the page answers not_checked_yet meanwhile. Fix round 2: only this situation, which passes by itself: send the same request again after the Runtime's next check.

root_failing.description: Fix round 2: the scheduler workbench checks the application's game root, and no check since the start could read it (its root files' metadata or their read fails; the page answers root_failing with the failure: the file, and the reader's first problem or the operating system's failure kind). Asking again does not help: the root must be repaired. No name can be set or cleared meanwhile, a resource goal that needs no declaration ({resource, at_least}) neither: while its root fails the game is uncomposed, so no goal of the application is in effect, and nothing is stored.

no_schedule.description: Fix round 2: the application's game has no standard pack root with schedule.json (the standard-pack root holds no game root for it, or its game root holds no schedule.json), so there is nothing to check: the composed catalog holds no rule and no pool of the game, no run reads a goal of it, and the page answers no_schedule. No name can be set or cleared, a resource goal that needs no declaration neither (no pool of the game is one the application can target), and nothing is stored; asking again does not help until the game root holds schedule.json.

confirmation_problem.description: What the program saw where the confirmation of the page a step awaits ended, or the declared error page a run stood on, the value confirmation_problem of page_confirmation_failed, contained_task_step_unconfirmed, contained_task_error_page_reached, contained_task_linear_unrecorded_screen and contained_task_requires_scheduler: one word per situation the kernel already tells apart there. It stands beside the code in the outcome's values and never in its detail text, so the failure identity, the streak and the frame rules stay as they are; for one code the program does the same next whichever word it carries (Workflow #469 V0, the owner's option A on board #469, since 0.12.62; the kernel slices set it).

input_not_taken.description: The program saw the step's own page at the end of the confirmation after the input and had seen no other page since the input (a linear step judges the frames in between, a page-graph step only the last frame): the input did not take; check its target and the gap before it.

returned_to_own_page.description: After the input the screen showed something else and was the step's own page again at the end: the input took and the screen came back; open the run's frames to see what was shown in between.

awaited_page_late.description: The awaited page appeared only after the confirmation wait: raise the step's timeout or check what slows the page.

other_page_shown.description: The screen settled on another page the package declares: declare that page as a destination or an interrupt.

loading_page_shown.description: The screen settled on a declared loading page: give the step more time or turn loading handling on.

transition_shown.description: The screen was still a loading transition when the wait ended.

interrupt_shown.description: A shared interrupt page was on screen and was not handled: check the interrupt's handling.

screen_moving.description: No declared page appeared and the screen kept changing: the step's timeout may be too short.

unrecorded_screen.description: The screen settled on a page the package never recorded: record that page in the package.

nothing_recognised.description: The last frame matched no declared page; open the run's frames to see what it showed.

screen_still.description: The screen stayed unchanged until the still limit: the input most likely did nothing.

final_state_unmet.description: The awaited page was on screen at the end but the state the step declares for it did not hold: check the step's final-state target and what the page showed.

wait_max_reached.description: The wait step's own page stayed on screen until its max_ms ran out and the awaited page did not come: raise max_ms or declare on_timeout.

loading_limit.description: The wait ended on its loading allowance while the screen was still loading.

error_page.description: The step reached a page the package declares as an error page.

error_page_no_exit.description: The run stood on a declared error page and no operation of the page leads away from it.

deadline_reached.description: The task's time ran out before the screen could be judged.

check_failed.description: The final look at the screen failed (capture or recognition); read the run's records.

neither_page.description: On the retry, neither the awaited page nor the step's own page appeared.

unjudged_layer_run.description: The screen was not judged after the wait: the run is a layer's (a prerequisite, return-home, navigation or recovery run) or one the host started, not the task's own; open the run's frames.

unjudged_restart_segment.description: The screen was not judged after the wait: the step ran inside an application restart; open the run's frames.

unjudged_consensus.description: The screen was not judged after the wait: the package declares sample consensus; open the run's frames.

unjudged_application_entry.description: The screen was not judged after the wait: the step is an application entry; open the run's frames.

unjudged_time_short.description: The screen was not judged after the wait: too little of the task's time was left (under twice the step timeout); open the run's frames.

guard_problem.description: Why an operation's guard refused its input, the value guard_problem of contained_task_guard_refused, with failure_code beside target_not_passed when the target's failure has a code: one word per situation. The program does the same next whichever word it is (Workflow #469 V0, the owner's option A on board #469, since 0.12.62; the kernel slices set it).

page_mismatch.description: The input was refused: the screen is not the page the operation's guard expects.

target_not_passed.description: The input was refused: the guard's target did not pass on its page (see failure_code).

page_moved.description: The page changed during the wait before a trusted-coordinate input.

availability_source.description: Who withdrew an application's availability, the value availability_source of instance_unavailable, read from the source of the active session.instance.available record that withdrew it and from the application's configured seed, with device_link_state or device_hold beside device_link and device_state. An application the configuration marks unavailable reads configured whichever publisher wrote the record that holds false, the self-check gate's withdrawal included (with no record holding false it reads facts_missing); self_check covers a self-check that failed, one not recorded yet (a failed preparation step included) or no longer valid, and a resource fence, which the gate withdraws under the same source. The application is held back at placement whichever word it is (Workflow #469 V0, the owner's option A on board #469, since 0.12.62; the host slice sets it).

configured.description: The configuration marks this application unavailable.

self_check.description: The device self-check has not passed (or the instance is fenced): see the instance's self-check and fence.

device_link.description: The handset's cable link is not connected (see device_link_state).

device_state.description: The handset is locked, too hot, low on battery or in use (see device_hold).

device_system.description: The handset's device system has no backend in this build (an iOS handset before its capture slice), so it is never available to policy (Workflow #479 F-2).

other_publisher.description: Another publisher marked the application unavailable.

facts_missing.description: The instance's facts are missing or unreadable.

pause_cause.description: Why a failure paused its task on the application, the value pause_cause of policy_task_paused, with failure_code the failure's code, chosen in the settlement's own order: a severe failure first, then a sensitive task, then the streak, then on_failure. The pair stays paused until its lift whichever word it is (Workflow #469 V0, the owner's option A on board #469, since 0.12.62; the host slice sets it).

severe_failure.description: The failure is one that pauses its task at the first occurrence. The pause lifts when the package changes; there is no manual lift.

unrecorded_screen.description: The package met a screen it never recorded. The pause lifts when the package changes; there is no manual lift.

runtime_budget_exceeded.description: The run took longer than its runtime budget. The pause lifts when the package changes; there is no manual lift.

interrupted_again.description: The run was cut short by the Runtime's own end twice in a row (the restart lifts only the first). The pause lifts when the package changes; there is no manual lift.

sensitive_task.description: A task marked sensitive failed; it pauses at once. The pause lifts when the package changes; there is no manual lift.

repeated_failure.description: The same failure repeated up to the task's threshold. The pause lifts when the package changes; there is no manual lift.

retries_exhausted.description: The task used up its retries and is set to pause on failure. The pause lifts when the package changes; there is no manual lift.

break_in_problem.description: What of a scheduled run's break-in could not be established before the run executed, the value break_in_problem of policy_break_in_unread, whose caused_by link is the failure behind it. The run is judged outside its break-in whichever word it is (Workflow #463 U1b fix round 3, contracts/policy-suspension.md "Only during a package's break-in", since 0.12.63).

content_unmeasured.description: The package's content was not measured when the run was prepared: the containment could not measure the package (caused_by its code when its refusal names one), or the Runtime clock, scheduling.suspension.lift_check_min_interval_ms or the lift checks' memory of the measurements could not be read. The run counts in no break-in.

record_unread.description: The pair's break-in could not be judged before the run executed: the decision memory does not hold the run's dispatch, or scheduling.suspension.break_in_runs, scheduling.suspension.break_in_ms or the Runtime clock could not be read. The run counts as any run of its content does.

trial_state_place.description: Where a state directory refused for trial records lies, the value trial_state_place of trial_state_dir_refused (Workflow #463 S3-10, contracts/standard-pack-trial.md "The record", since 0.12.64).

repository.description: It is, or lies inside, a Git work tree: a directory along its path holds .git.

installed_root.description: It is, or lies inside, an installed root: a directory along its path whose install\state.json is a file, the installer's own state file in both layouts (contracts/install-cli.md, fix round 2).

trial_record_problem.description: Why a file of a trial record's name is not read as that record, the value trial_record_problem of trial_record_unreadable (Workflow #463 S3-10 fix round 2, contracts/standard-pack-trial.md "The record", since 0.12.64).

read_failed.description: The operating system refused to open or read the file, or to list its directory; its refusal is the cause.

too_large.description: The file is larger than 1 MiB, the most a record is read up to.

undecodable.description: The file does not decode as actingcommand.pack-trial.v1; the decoder's refusal is the cause.

name_mismatch.description: The file decodes, but is not the record of the package, the content and the time its name says.

trial_collect_problem.description: Why the run a trial's --collect names is not a run of the trial, the value trial_collect_problem of trial_collect_mismatch (Workflow #463 S3-11, contracts/standard-pack-trial.md "Reading the end later", since 0.12.65).

other_package.description: The run's facts do not name the trial's package as the package it admitted: they name another one, or none.

other_instance.description: The run's facts do not name the instance the trial is for: they name another one, or none.

scheduled.description: Fix round 2: the run is the scheduler's (dispatch scheduled); a trial's run is sent by hand.

origin_unknown.description: Fix round 2: the run's facts hold no record of its request's origin (dispatch unknown), so whether it was sent by hand is not known.

other_channel.description: Fix round 2: the run was sent by hand on another channel than the Lab's (origin cli or ui); a trial's run is sent on the Lab's channel.

trial_run_unconfirmed.description: What the answer of a trial's run knows of a run the Runtime confirmed nothing of, the member next.unconfirmed, said in the place of the line that reads the end later (next.collect), which such a run may never have (Workflow #463 S3-8, S3-9 fix round 1, contracts/standard-pack-trial.md "The run", since 0.12.68).

no_receipt.description: The run's request was written and the connection that carried it ended before any of its receipt came back: the Runtime confirmed nothing of the run, and whether it was accepted or started is not known. A Runtime below runtime-client revision 11 ends the connection so on a run with values, running nothing; one that stopped while the run was in it ends it too. No record is written.

trial_state.description: The latest trial of a content as the trial records of the state directory keep it, the state of the one summary of a content's trials: the member review.trial.state of standard-pack adopt (Workflow #463 S3-12, contracts/standard-pack-authoring.md "The trial and the two warnings") and trial.state of standard-pack status (S3-14, contracts/standard-pack-schedule.md "Where a pack stands"); each record judged as contracts/standard-pack-trial.md "The record" defines a trial that passed (the train of S3-12 and S3-14, since 0.12.68).

passed.description: The latest record of this content passed, as contracts/standard-pack-trial.md "The record" defines it: its run ended on an end the package declares (end.outcome success) and, when the trial was given an expectation (--expect), on that end (matched not false).

failed.description: The latest record of this content did not pass: its run failed or was cancelled, or ended normally on another end than the one the trial expected (matched false). passed_on_record says whether an earlier record of it passed.

none.description: No record of this content is on record; a record of another content of the same package counts for nothing (other_content says whether there is one).

stage_state.description: Where a pack stands in stage three of package making, the member stage_state of standard-pack status and the counts stage_states, saying only what the row knows (Workflow #463 S3-14 and the train of S3-12 and S3-14, contracts/standard-pack-schedule.md "Where a pack stands", since 0.12.68).

not_admitted.description: Its readiness item S1 does not hold: the Runtime's loader, or standard-pack check, refuses its admission.

not_judged.description: The train of S3-12 and S3-14: admitted, and the composer refuses the root's schedule.json (enabled.state not_judged); the Runtime keeps the last schedule it accepted, which this root does not tell.

can_be_tried.description: Admitted, and nothing of the root's accepted schedule.json enables it: it is held (enabled.state held) or no rule names it (not_placed).

supporting.description: The train of S3-12 and S3-14: admitted, and it plays a supporting part a root file gives it, used by other packs' runs, and no rule names it (enabled.state not_scheduled).

enabled.description: Admitted, and a rule of the root's schedule.json enables it (enabled.state enabled).

enabled_state.description: Whether the root's schedule.json enables a pack, judged from the classification its readiness item S2 reads, the member enabled.state of standard-pack status and the counts enabled_states (Workflow #463 S3-14, contracts/standard-pack-schedule.md "Where a pack stands", since 0.12.68).

enabled.description: A rule names it and it is not held: the scheduler dispatches it by that rule, whatever supporting part it plays beside.

held.description: schedule.json holds it, and no root file gives it a supporting part.

not_placed.description: No rule names it, it is not held and no root file gives it a supporting part, or the root holds no schedule.json: nothing places it into scheduling.

not_scheduled.description: It plays a supporting part a root file gives it and no rule dispatches it (the readiness's not_scheduled).

not_judged.description: The composer refuses the root's schedule.json, so no rule is classified (S2 composition_refused); the Runtime keeps the last schedule it accepted, which this root does not tell.

pack_authorization.description: What standard-pack status says of the authorization a pack was enabled under, the member enabled.authorization (Workflow #463 S3-14, contracts/standard-pack-schedule.md "Where a pack stands", since 0.12.68).

not_recorded.description: No placement journal read names the pack; enabled.authorization_unrecorded says why. The tool never infers an authorization.

authorization_unrecorded.description: Why standard-pack status records no authorization for a pack, the member enabled.authorization_unrecorded (Workflow #463 S3-14, contracts/standard-pack-schedule.md "Where a pack stands", since 0.12.68; one word per cause since Workflow #463 S3-15a, 0.12.69).

journals_not_read.description: The placement journals were not read: the row was not asked to read the installation (--installation).

no_journal_names_it.description: Workflow #463 S3-15a: every journal of the installation was read and no placement that counts names the pack in its input enabled: none that finished with every item placed and was neither undone nor rolled back.

journals_unreadable.description: Workflow #463 S3-15a: no journal that was read names the pack, and some journals could not be read (the root's installation.operations_unread): one of them may name it.

pairs_unread.description: Why standard-pack status --installation answers no pairs: each pack's pairs in place of its list, and the root's installation.pairs_unread beside the outcome that says why (Workflow #463 S3-15a, contracts/standard-pack-schedule.md "Where a pack stands", since 0.12.69).

suspension_report_not_read.description: The installation's actingd suspended gave no report: it could not be started, it failed or printed no report, it read another state root, or it was ended at its deadline; the outcome beside it is the one a diagnosis gives the same child.

bindings_not_read.description: The report was read, but the composed bindings that name the package each catalog task runs could not be read (actingctl packs' reading of the installation's configuration); its refusal is the outcome beside it.

no_task_bound.description: Fix round 1 (0.12.69): the report and the composed bindings were read, and the bindings hold no task that runs this pack (a configuration that binds its procedures itself, whose rows name no task; a game the composition left out, its warnings in the answer's warnings; a pack no composed rule runs), so no row of the report can be the pack's. A pack's own word in its pairs, never the root's installation.pairs_unread.

drop_problem.description: Why record mark's drop_step does not drop a step before the last of a Lab recording, the value drop_problem of record_drop_unproven (#463 S2-7, contracts/lab-recording.md "Steps, frames and remediation", since 0.12.68): the stored frames do not hold what the comparison needs, or they show a change, or (#463 KR-1 fix round 1, since 0.12.70) the step's effect is a declared key. Fix round 1: two frames are the same screen when two comparisons hold, the whole frame and the neighbourhood of the press (its rectangle grown by one cell of the whole-frame grid on every side), each by the measure stage one calls a screen still by, frame_change_milli at most FRAME_CHANGE_MAX_MILLI (1500); a change smaller than that measure sees is not seen, and whether the press mattered is the agent's judgement.

frames_not_recorded.description: The step has no press on record with the stored frame it was sent on and the stored frame after it (no click performed by tap, swipe or long-tap --record, a press sent on a capture that was not stored, an application operation), or a frame the comparison needs is not on record.

screen_changed.description: The stored frames show a change: the frame after the press differs from the frame before it by more than the frame-change bound, by one of the two comparisons (drop_comparison).

next_screen_differs.description: The stored frames show a change: the next step's frame before its press differs from the frame before this press by more than the frame-change bound, by one of the two comparisons (drop_comparison).

key_declared.description: #463 KR-1 fix round 1 (since 0.12.70): the step's effect is a declared key: the frames on record are those of the press the key replaced, and nothing shows what the key does; the key is taken back first (key false, --no-key).

drop_comparison.description: Which of the two comparisons of two stored frames showed the change for which record mark's drop_step refuses a step before the last, the value drop_comparison of record_drop_unproven beside drop_problem screen_changed or next_screen_differs (#463 S2-7 fix round 1, contracts/lab-recording.md "Steps, frames and remediation", since 0.12.68). The whole frame is compared first.

frame.description: The whole frame, by the frame-change measure (a grid of 16 by 9 cells over the frame, the mean colour of each cell).

press_region.description: The neighbourhood of the press: its rectangle (a point is a rectangle of one pixel, a swipe the rectangle spanned by its two ends) grown on every side by one cell of the whole-frame grid at the recording's size and clamped to the frame, by the same measure over that region.

scan_problem.description: Why the swipes recorded before a press of a Lab recording cannot be folded into one scrolling search of that press, the fold undone, a step of a fold acted on, or the fold generated, the value scan_problem of record_scan_invalid (#463 S2-8', contracts/lab-recording.md "Folding swipes into a scrolling search", since 0.12.70). A swipe runs clearly along one axis when its move along it, between its own two points, is not zero and at least twice its move across it.

fold_range_invalid.description: fold_scan names no fold: its first step is not below its press step; a step of the range is unknown, dropped, converted into a transition, or folded or holding a fold already; the press step's effect is no executed tap; or a step between them is no executed swipe.

inserted_in_range.description: #463 S2-8' fix round 1: a step of the range, the press step included, is an optional step a stopped recording inserted after the stop, no step recorded on the path.

would_lose_marks.description: A step the fold would fold has marks of its own, which no page of the package would read any more.

would_lose_page.description: A step the fold would fold names its page.

would_lose_optional.description: A step the fold would fold is optional.

would_lose_choice.description: A step the fold would fold holds a choice (marked as holding one, or refined by a select).

would_lose_transition.description: A step the fold would fold has a transition after its effect.

would_lose_inserted.description: #463 S2-8' fix round 1: a step the fold would fold has an optional step a stopped recording inserted after it after the stop, and not given up, which would run after no step of the package.

move_axis_unclear.description: A swipe of the range runs clearly along neither axis (its move along one axis is not at least twice its move across it), or along another axis than the first swipe.

move_after_back.description: A swipe in the first swipe's direction after one against it: the demonstration goes forward as often as needed, then back as often as needed, then presses.

not_folded.description: unfold_scan names a step that holds no fold.

step_in_fold.description: A step action or a mark names a step of a fold: a swipe folded into a press step, or (a step action) the press step that holds the fold; the fold is undone first.

scan_not_selected.description: record stop meets a press step whose swipes are folded into it and which declares no scrolling select yet, so its package would press without scrolling.

scan_selected.description: unfold_scan names a press step whose fold a scrolling select reads; the select is taken off first, with clear_select (#463 S2-9a).

end_not_recorded.description: record stop meets a scrolling select that reads its list to its end and declares no end mark: the demonstration never reached the list's end (#463 S2-9a).

privacy_rect_kind.description: Which rectangle of a package a privacy finding names, the value privacy_rect_kind of the privacy_ codes: the kind of a region of the one list of a package's read regions, or a rectangle of a regression case's scene (#463 PRIV-1, contracts/privacy-zones.md, since 0.12.74).

template_search.description: A template target's search area, its region, which holds the template's crop (with the margin record mark gives a search area it is not told).

color_check.description: A template target's colour check region.

ocr.description: An OCR target's region, when no candidate layout reads the target as a feature.

shared_ocr.description: A candidate layout's shared OCR read, shared_ocr.region as declared (a fixed_slots layout's, or since #463 SEL-2L-b a repeated_anchor layout's); the finding's target is the layout's id.

select_name.description: An OCR target a candidate layout reads as a feature (a fixed_slots slot's targets, a feature's target), and none as an integer: a select's name region.

select_quantity.description: An OCR target a candidate layout reads as an integer feature (ocr_integer): a select's quantity column, the integer column a read_list step publishes into its list; the kernel reads it as a number, so such a region is a reading (fix rounds 1 and 2).

scene_rect.description: A rectangle of a regression case's scene, scene_construction.rects.

privacy_zone_kind.description: What a sensitive zone of privacy-zones.json holds, a zone's kind and the value privacy_zone_kind of privacy_zone_met (#463 PRIV-1 amendment 1, the owner's ruling of 11-18, since 0.12.74).

identity.description: Who the account is (a nickname, an account number, a server name): nothing may read there. A zone that declares no kind is of this kind.

value.description: A quantity the account holds: only a reading, a region the kernel reads as a number at run time, may read there, and no scene may hold its pixels.

privacy_unseen_kind.description: What a rectangle check of a package cannot see, the kinds of the value privacy_unseen_counts of privacy_unseen (#463 PRIV-1, since 0.12.74).

expected_text.description: A text an OCR target of the package expects (its expected values): a text is no rectangle.

alias.description: An alias an identity entry of a candidate layout of the package is read as.

case_other_schema.description: A regression case of another schema than actingcommand.resource-regression-case.v1, or of none, whose scene's rectangles were not read.

idle_wake_cause.description: Why an idle instance's wake was queued, the value idle_wake_cause of instance_idle_action with operation queue_idle_wake, the first that holds in the vocabulary's order (#484 IDLE-W2, contracts/runtime-config.md "What wakes an idle instance", since 0.12.75).

task_due.description: The scheduler's latest plan shows a task of the instance due that can be dispatched now: selected, or eligible with no wake of its own later than the evaluation and nothing after a hold of the instance holding it back; the record names it as task_id (a catalog task's id, nothing of an account).

action_changed.description: The idle action in effect is no longer the one taken on the instance (under auto: the tier taken is no longer one auto allows on it).

owed_at_start.description: The start owed the wake: the instance was restored woken whose startup package had not run, or restored closed from no usable record of what the idle action left, its wake at the start's time.

planned_time_reached.description: The planned wake time, the next due task's time less the action's wake lead, was reached (also while a pause, an install hold or a claim held the instance, whose claims then wait behind the holder).
